=== PAGE 10 ===
SUMMARY
This summary aims to give you an overview of the information contained in this
prospectus. As this is a summary, it does not contain all the information that may be important
to you. You should read this prospectus in its entirety before you decide to invest in the Offer
Shares.
There are risks associated with any investment. Some of the particular risks in investing
in the Offer Shares are set out in “Risk Factors” in this prospectus. You should read that
section carefully before you decide to invest in the Offer Shares.
Who WeAre
We focus on electronic ceramic materials and components, with over fifty-five years of
operating history. We have concentrated on electronic ceramic materials and components
throughout our history. We have built a product portfolio across four categories — electronic and
ceramic materials, electronic components, telecommunication (“telecom”) components and
equipment components — forming a business framework that spans foundational materials,
critical components and high-end devices and assemblies across key application areas including
telecom, AI and data centers, consumer electronics, automotive electronics, semiconductor
manufacturing and packaging, new energy and intelligent industrial control.
We operate an integrated business model across materials and processes. Specifically, we
possess solid R&D capabilities in critical upstream raw materials formulations and implement
iterative optimization of technological processes of key manufacturing stages. At the same time,
we have large batch production capabilities with high-standard quality control, reinforcing core
advantages in supply and cost controllability.
Our R&D organization includes research institutes and business-unit technical teams,
covering raw material formulation as well as forming and sintering processes. We hold numerous
patents and participate in formulation and revision of various industry standards. We seek to
translate materials and process R&D into manufacturable product platforms. Regarding
production, we have multiple domestic production bases and strategic overseas sites enabling
cross-base capacity allocation, complemented by a sales network covering key global markets.
With respect to customers, we maintain long-term relationships with key customers across
our primary end markets, integrating localized services with global standards to strengthen
customer stickiness.
We have developed a diversified product portfolio that integrates mature product lines with
high-growth potential offerings. This matrix enables us to stabilize our revenue base while
capturing growth opportunities across core business scenarios. Regarding management, our
experienced and stable management team, together with a system covering systems,
mechanisms and culture, provides strong support for our continued focus on the electronic
ceramic materials business.

Electronic and Ceramic Materials
We focus on upstream foundational materials for the electronics value chain. Our portfolio
includes alumina (aluminum oxide) ceramic substrates, aluminum nitride ceramic substrates,
electronic pastes and solid oxide fuel cell (“SOFC”) electrolyte sheets.
As core upstream materials, these products are deployed across consumer electronics,
automotive electronics and new energy applications. Together, these products support electronic
component manufacturing and new-energy fuel cell applications. In particular:
• alumina ceramic substrates are used as base materials for chip resistors in consumer
electronics, providing electrical insulation, heat dissipation and mechanical support;
• electronic paste series — including resistive, mask, conductor and G2 encapsulated
pastes — are used for electrode printing in precision electronic components; and
• SOFC electrolyte sheets enable oxygen-ion transport while isolating fuel and oxidant,
facilitating direct electrochemical conversion of chemical energy to electricity under
high-temperature conditions and serving as a core component for SOFCs.
During the Track Record Period, our revenue from sales of electronic and ceramic materials
amounted to RMB1,548.7 million, RMB1,677.2 million and RMB1,959.4 million in 2023, 2024 and
2025, respectively, accounting for 27.3%, 23.1% and 22.1% of our total revenue in the same
years.
Electronic Components
Our electronic components portfolio comprises multilayer ceramic chip capacitors
(“MLCCs”), multilayer ceramic chip inductors (“MLCIs”) and fixed resistors. Capacitors, inductors
and resistors are foundational passive components broadly used across electronic circuits.
MLCCs are currently the primary revenue driver within this category. Leveraging our technical
capabilities accumulated over the years and our continued investment in R&D, we have
expanded our product lineup and scaled up supply to support diverse applications, while
supplying MLCCs, MLCIs and resistors in a coordinated manner to meet customers' one-stop
procurement service needs and enhance the compatibility of multi-category components.
– 4 –

=== PAGE 14 ===
SUMMARY
Demand growth has been supported by technology iteration and application upgrades,
particularly inAI and data centers and automotive electronics, according to Frost & Sullivan. This
has increased requirements for high-end passive components.
We focus on technology, delivery, customer access and capacity:
• Technology. Our high-end MLCCs have achieved a dielectric layer thickness of
approximately one micrometer and stacking layers exceeding 1,000, laying the
foundation for our entry into advanced application scenarios includingAI data centers,
automotive electronics and semiconductors.
• Delivery. We rely on highly automated, end-to-end production to support the delivery
of large orders with stable quality.
• Customers. We have obtained certifications from key customers across various core
downstream scenarios.
• Capacity. We have expanded our production capacity as our orders increase and have
achieved large-scale mass production.
We believe that our success in these aspects enables us to benefit from industry growth and
market share gains.
Telecom Components
We focus on core needs in optical communication components and semiconductor-related
packaging, and have formed a diversified product matrix covering optical interconnects,
packaging parts as well as crystal oscillator packaging. Our portfolio includes ceramic ferrules
and sleeves, ceramic packages (“PKGs”), mechanical transfer (“MT”) ferrules and MT short
jumpers, and optical communication ceramic packages. These products correspond to different
key nodes in the communications value chain and together constitute our comprehensive supply
capabilities in telecom,AI and data centers, and semiconductor manufacturing and packaging.
Our telecom component product offering is a core lever for consolidating our position in
optical communications while expanding into semiconductor manufacturing and packaging.
• Ceramic ferrules and sleeves provide high-precision alignment to reduce signal loss
for high-speed broadband access, enabling precise fiber mating and serving
fiber-to-the-home (“FTTH”), 5G telecom base stations and data centers.
• In response to the high-density, high-bandwidth interconnect needs arising from the
rapid growth of AI and data centers. MT ferrules and MT short jumpers offer
low-latency, high-reliability optical communication solutions and act as key enablers of
the digital economy.
• Meanwhile, our PKGs address the high hermeticity and stability packaging
requirements of crystal oscillator whose downstream applications span automobiles,
smartphones, telecom base stations and laptops.
As end devices in segments such as automotive and IoT continue to become more
intelligent and connected, demand for crystal oscillator is increasing, which in turn supports
sustained growth in PKG demand, according to Frost & Sullivan.

SUMMARY
Our revenue from sales of telecom components amounted to RMB1,766.8 million,
RMB2,306.0 million and RMB2,594.3 million in 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively, accounting for
31.1%, 31.7% and 29.3% of our total revenue in the same years.
Our telecom components have established notable competitiveness.
• According to Frost & Sullivan, our ceramic ferrules and sleeves accounted for
approximately 70% of the global market in terms of revenue in 2025;
• According to Frost & Sullivan, our PKGs accounted for approximately 40% of the
global market in crystal oscillator packaging in terms of revenue in 2025;
• Our MT ferrules and MT short jumpers as well as optical communication ceramic
packages are gradually entering the supply chains of high-speed optical modules and
high-end optical devices.
Equipment Components
Our equipment components portfolio includes piezo microdispensing systems,
pan-semiconductor ceramic components, hermetic terminal for compressors, ceramic capillaries
and SOFC stacks. Drawing on accumulated core technologies in materials formulation and
forming capabilities, we provide products that address localization and energy-transition needs
while also serving steady industrial demand.
These products are used across several areas such as semiconductor manufacturing and
packaging, new energy and intelligent industrial control.
• Hermetic terminal for compressors deliver high hermetic sealing and dielectric strength
for compressors used in air conditioners, refrigerators and vehicles;
• Ceramic capillaries are bonding tools used in wire bonders for semiconductor
packaging;
• SOFC stacks extend from our SOFC accumulated expertise in this field and are
designed for distributed power generation;
• Pan-semiconductor ceramic components meet the high requirements for purity and
precision by advanced manufacturing; and
• Piezo microdispensing systems fulfill precision dispensing requirements in industrial
automation and robotics.
Other Products
Beyond our core product offerings, we leverage materials and process know-how to extend
product development into additional applications, primarily including ceramic appearance parts
and bioceramics. These extensions complement our core product portfolio and broaden our
market opportunities.

Our Growth Opportunities
We operate in industries and markets in which demand growth has been supported by
technological iteration and application upgrades. This has consistently increased requirements
for high-end passive components. According to Frost & Sullivan, the global markets for core
electronic ceramic materials, core ceramic electronic components, core ceramic telecom
components and core ceramic equipment components are projected to grow from 2026 at a
CAGR of 11.6%, 7.2%, 9.2% and 11.9%, to reach RMB43.1 billion, RMB256.8 billion, RMB75.9
billion and RMB98.6 billion by 2030, respectively. We believe the key growth drivers of our
business include:
• Demand and scenario upgrades in downstream sectors. Telecom, AI and data
centers, consumer and automotive electronics, semiconductors, new energy, and
intelligent industrial control are simultaneously upgrading, driving higher volumes and
tighter performance requirements through premiumization in consumer electronics,
widespread adoption of AI and IoT, electrification and intelligence of vehicles, global
expansion of computing infrastructure, deepened domestic substitution in
semiconductors and the energy transition. This underpins sustained, multi-year
industry growth. For example, for telecom sector, by 2030, the number of global 5G/6G
base stations is expected to reach over 20 million units, while for AI and data centers
sector, global data center capital expenditure is projected to grow from over USD500
billion in 2025 to over USD3 trillion by 2030. As AI data centers evolve towards larger
scale and higher power density, the power density per rack has increased from under
10kW to over 120kW, requiring higher performance of materials and components.
Regarding consumer electronics sector, driven by the integration of innovative
products and the accelerated adoption of AI applications, global shipments of
consumer electronics products are projected to increase from 2.2 billion units in 2025
to approximately 2.7 billion units by 2030. And in terms of automotive electronics
sector, it is expected that global sales volume of NEVs will increase from nearly 24
million units in 2025 to over 40 million units by 2030.
• Higher material performance requirements and functional integration. High-end
scenarios demand higher thermal conductivity, dielectric stability, purity, and reliability
under extreme conditions. In parallel, ceramics are integrating multiple functions such
as heat dissipation, structural strength, and electrical performance to support
miniaturized, compact product designs.
• Fundamental R&D and cross-sector innovation. Foundational materials science
combined with application know-how in semiconductors, new energy, and healthcare
— often through industry-academia collaboration — accelerates lab-to-fab transfer,
breaks performance bottlenecks, and opens new use cases.
• Domestic substitution and global-local operating models. Policy support and
strong local demand accelerate domestic substitution across materials, components,
and equipment, expanding market share for domestic players. Backed by domestic
industrial clusters, overseas manufacturing sites, and local technical service teams,
our global network, paired with customized regional adaptation strategies, enhances
compliance efficiency, optimizes cost structure, shortens delivery lead times, and
mitigates potential trade and policy risks.

Our Management and Corporate Culture
With over half a century of commitment in electronic ceramics, we have developed a
management and corporate culture aligned with our materials-centric business approach. Such
approach anchors strategic direction in core values while relying on institutionalized
management to support execution efficiency.
On operations, we focus on our principal business with a disciplined and pragmatic
approach. We leverage digital systems to connect end-to-end operating processes and use
standardization to support efficiency. Our performance assessments and incentive mechanisms
are results-oriented and emphasize both steady achievement of business objectives and
collaborative capability building across teams. Dedicated mechanisms are in place to encourage
R&D innovation, reinforcing a virtuous cycle between technology advancement and talent
development.
Culturally, we not only emphasize respect for professionalism and commitment to quality,
promote the collaborative sharing and reuse of technology and resources with an open mindset,
but also attach importance to building a growth platform for employees, forging team synergy
while supporting individual development.
These practices align with our long-term objectives: to provide solutions that address
customer requirements, to build development pathways for employees, to create value for
shareholders, and to contribute to society. We aim to embed steady growth and pursuit of
excellence into daily operations to navigate industry cycles and market changes.
We value long-term support from shareholders and investors. Since the listing of our A
Shares on the ChiNext of the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in December 2014, we have maintained
a relatively high dividend payout.As of December 31, 2025, our cumulative cash dividends since
the listing of our A Shares totaled RMB4,803.5 million. Our dividend payout ratios (calculated as
cash dividends declared for the relevant year divided by net profit attributable to the parent) were
33.9%, 33.2% and 32.8% for 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively. In addition, we have
implemented share repurchase programs in response to market dynamics to further enhance
shareholder returns. We launched our first share repurchase program in April 2025. As of the
Latest Practicable Date, the total amount used for share repurchases reached RMB175.4 million
and our share repurchase program had been completed.
Financial Performance
Since the listing of our A Shares on the ChiNext of the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2014,
we have recorded steady revenue growth and maintained solid profitability. Our revenue was
RMB5,681.5 million, RMB7,266.1 million and RMB8,868.5 million in 2023, 2024 and 2025,
respectively. Our gross profit was RMB2,154.1 million, RMB2,975.3 million and RMB3,542.8
million for the same years. Our net profit was RMB1,583.2 million, RMB2,190.2 million and
RMB2,617.0 million, and our net cash generated from operating activities was RMB1,719.0
million, RMB2,403.1 million and RMB2,877.6 million for the same years, respectively. We believe
these results reflect our capability in sustainable value creation over the long term.
We are seeking a listing on the Exchange to: (i) broaden our access to international equity
capital markets and diversify funding channels for potential capacity expansion, selected
overseas site build-outs and R&D investments; (ii) enhance our international visibility and brand
recognition among global customers and suppliers in key application sectors; and (iii) facilitate
potential strategic collaborations, talent recruitment under an internationally recognized listing
framework.

SUMMARY
RESEARCHAND DEVELOPMENT
We compete in a market characterized by rapid technology iteration, increasingly stringent
reliability standards and persistent cost reduction pressure, which subjects our R&D to
heightened challenges and requirements. Leveraging years of accumulated technological
know-how and large-scale mass production experience, we have established a tiered R&D
system featuring four layers — “one generation in mass production, one in reserve, one in
development and one in research,” — to systematically respond to rapid shifts in market and
industry demand.
SALESAND MARKETING
As of December 31, 2025, our sales team consisted of 208 dedicated sales personnel
covering eight countries and regions, with on-the-ground deployment and team build-outs
completed in each of these markets. Our products are sold through both direct sales and
distributors, among which MLCCs, piezo microdispensing systems and alumina ceramic
substrates are sold through both direct sales and distributors, and other types of products are
sold to direct sales customers.
CUSTOMERSAND SUPPLIERS
Our Customers
We sell our products to new energy equipment, electronic component and consumer
electronic devices manufacturers. During the Track Record Period, our products were sold in the
PRC, as well as to NorthAmerica,Asia, Europe and other regions around the world.
Sales to our five largest customers in each year during Track Record Period amounted to
RMB1,005.1 million, RMB1,016.9 million and RMB1,345.3 million, accounting for 17.6%, 14.0%
and 15.2% of our total revenue for respective year. Sales to our largest customer in each year
during Track Record Period amounted to RMB449.3 million, RMB323.9 million and RMB330.7
million, accounting for 7.9%, 4.5% and 3.7% of our total revenue for respective year.
During the Track Record Period, to the best knowledge of our Directors, none of our
Directors, their associates or any of our Shareholders (who, to the knowledge of our Directors,
own more than 5% of our share capital) had any interest in our five largest customers in each
year during the Track Record Period that is required to be disclosed under the Hong Kong Listing
Rules.
Our Suppliers
We have established a comprehensive system for the selection and qualification of
suppliers to ensure the stability and reliability of our supply chain.
Purchases from our five largest suppliers in each year during Track Record Period
amounted to RMB505.8 million, RMB829.7 million and RMB1,005.8 million, accounting for
22.1%, 26.0% and 26.7% of our total revenue for respective year. Purchases from our largest
supplier in each year during Track Record Period amounted to RMB130.0 million, RMB242.2
million and RMB252.5 million, accounting for 5.7%, 7.6% and 6.7% of our total revenue for
respective year.

Our revenue increased by 22.1% from RMB7,266.1 million in 2024 to RMB8,868.5 million in
2025. More specifically, our revenue from sales of electronic and ceramic materials increased by
16.8% from RMB1,677.2 million in 2024 to RMB1,959.4 million in 2025, primarily due to the
increase in average selling price from RMB686.4 per unit to RMB854.4 per unit, which in turn
reflects an increase in price of raw materials and a change in our product mix whereby resulted in
revenue contribution from certain higher-value materials increased due to strong demand. Our
revenue from sales of electronic components increased by 43.9% from RMB2,298.2 million in
2024 to RMB3,308.1 million in 2025, primarily due to the increase in sales volume from 33.7
million units to 48.8 million units, reflecting stronger downstream demand for MLCCs in consumer
electronics, home appliances, AI and data centers, and automotive electronics, as well as
customers’increased preference for localized products amid geopolitical and policy factors.
Our revenue increased by 27.9% from RMB5,681.5 million in 2023 to RMB7,266.1 million in
2024. More specifically, our revenue from sales of electronic and ceramic materials increased by
8.3% from RMB1,548.7 million in 2023 to RMB1,677.2 million in 2024, primarily due to an
increase in average selling price from RMB588.7 per unit to RMB686.4 per unit, as we increased
our selling price in response to a change in product mix and to a lesser extent, an increase in
price of raw materials. Our revenue from sales of electronic components increased by 46.2%
from RMB1,572.3 million in 2023 to RMB2,298.2 million in 2024, primarily due to the increase in
sales volume from 24.5 million units to 33.7 million units, which was driven by increase in our
market share of MLCCs in downstream industries. Our revenue from sales of telecom
components increased by 30.5% from RMB1,766.8 million in 2023 to RMB2,306.0 million in
2024, primarily due to an increase in both sales volume and average selling price, reflecting
increase in market demand and favorable product mix.
In 2023, 2024 and 2025, revenue generated from sales to the United States amounted to
RMB484.0 million, RMB414.1 million and RMB487.8 million, representing 8.5%, 5.7% and 5.5%
of our total revenue, respectively.The decrease on our revenue from the United States from 2023
to 2024 were primarily due to changes in demands for electronic and ceramic materials, while the
increase on our revenue from the United States from 2024 to 2025 were mainly due to changes in
demands for telecom components and equipment components inAI and data center sectors.

manufacturing overheads, alongside a richer sales mix. Our gross profit from sales of telecom
components increased from RMB702.7 million in 2023 to RMB977.4 million in 2024, primarily due
to the increase in revenue. Gross margin increased from 39.8% to 42.4%. The margin
improvement reflected stronger market demand for ceramic ferrules and PKG products used in
data centers and 5G deployments.
See “Financial Information — Year-to-Year Comparison of Results of Operations.”

LISTING EXPENSES
Listing expenses represent professional fees, underwriting commission and fees incurred in
connection with the Listing and the Global Offering. Our listing expenses are estimated to be
approximately HK$111.9 million (including underwriting commission) accounting for 1.6% of the
gross proceeds of the Global Offering, assuming that the maximum Offer Price of HK$100.30 per
Share.Among our listing expenses, approximately HK$103.3 million is directly attributable to the
issuance of Shares and will be charged to equity upon completion of the Listing, and
approximately HK$8.6 million has been or will be charged to our consolidated statement of
comprehensive income. The listing expenses we incurred in the Track Record Period and expect
to incur would consist of approximately HK$72.2 million underwriting related expenses and fees
(including underwriting commissions, SFC transaction levy, Stock Exchange trading fee and
AFRC transaction levy), approximately HK$28.7 million non-underwriting-related expenses and
fees including fees for the Sole Sponsor, legal advisors and reporting accountant and
approximately HK$11.0 million for other non-underwriting-related fees and expenses. During the
Track Record Period, we incurred RMB11.6 million in listing expenses, among which RMB1.4
million was charged to profit and loss and RMB10.2 million will be charged to equity upon
completion of the listing.
The listing expenses above are the latest practicable estimate for reference only, and the
actual amount may differ from this estimate.

RISK FACTORS
We face risks including those set out in the section headed “Risk Factors.” As different
investors may have different interpretations and criteria when determining the significance of
risks, you should read the “Risk Factors” section in its entirety before you decide to invest in our
H Shares. Some of the major risks that we face include:
• our business is exposed to supply–demand dynamics in the electronic ceramic
material and component industry and affected by downstream demand for end
products in which our materials and components are used.
• if we are unable to retain existing customers or attract new customers, our business,
financial condition and results of operations may be adversely affected.
• our international strategy and ability to conduct business in various jurisdictions is
subject to uncertainties and risks.
• fluctuations in the prices of raw materials may adversely affect our profitability and
financial condition.
• we source raw materials externally, and we may not be able to secure our supply of
such materials in a stable and timely manner.
• We may be subject to the risks associated with international trade policies, geopolitics
measures, and investment restrictions.

DIVIDEND POLICY
Subject to PRC laws and regulations, including the PRC Company Law 《( 中華人民共和國公
司法》) and the No. 3 Guideline for the Supervision of Listed Companies — Cash Dividend
Distribution of Listed Companies (2025 Revision) 《( 上市公司監管指引第3號 — 上市公司現金分
紅(2025年修訂)》), and the Articles of Association, after taking into account the characteristics of
the industry in which we operate, our stage of development, our business model, profitability,
whether there are plans for significant capital expenditure and other factors, we have adopted a
formal dividend policy, under which we prioritize cash distributions. The Company shall distribute
a cash dividend in any year it is profitable and has distributable profits after making up for
previous years’losses and allocating to the required statutory reserves.
Profit distributions shall not exceed the aggregate amount of cumulative distributable
profits. In the absence of any material investment plan or significant capital expenditure
arrangement, the cash dividends distributed by us shall be no less than 30.0% of the distributable
profits realized for that year.
A material investment plan or significant capital expenditure arrangement refers to either of
the following circumstances:
(i) The cumulative expenditure on outbound investments, asset acquisitions, equipment
purchases or similar transactions planned by the Company within the next 12 months
reaches or exceeds 50% of the Company’s most recently audited net assets, and the
absolute amount exceeds RMB50 million.
(ii) The cumulative expenditure on outbound investments, asset acquisitions, equipment
purchases or similar transactions planned by the Company within the next 12 months
reaches or exceeds 30% of the Company’s most recently audited total assets.
Subsequent to the end of the Track Record Period, a final dividend in respect of the year
ended December 31, 2025 of RMB0.45 per share (inclusive of tax), in aggregate of
RMB860,114,000 (excluding the treasury shares), was approved by our shareholders at the
general meeting onApril 20, 2026 and paid subsequently.
See Note 13 to “Appendix I — Accountants’ Report” for our declared dividends during the
Track Record Period.
Future profit distributions may be carried out in the form of cash dividends or stock
dividends or a combination of cash dividends and stock dividends. Any proposed distribution of
dividends is subject to the discretion of our Board and the approval at our Shareholders’
meetings. Our Board may recommend a distribution of dividends in the future after taking into
account our results of operations, financial condition, operating requirements, capital
requirements, shareholders’ interests and any other conditions that our Board may deem
relevant.

RISK FACTORS
An investment in the H Shares involves various risks. You should consider carefully all
the information set out in this document and, in particular, the risks described below before
making an investment in the H Shares.
The occurrence of any of the following events could materially and adversely affect our
business, financial position, results of operations or prospects. If any of these events occurs,
the trading price of the H Shares could decline and you may lose all or part of your investment.
This document also contains forward-looking information that involves risks and uncertainties.
Our actual results could differ materially from those anticipated in these forward-looking
statements as a result of many factors, including the risks described below. You should seek
professional advice from your relevant advisors regarding your prospective investment in the
context of your particular circumstances.
RISKS RELATING TO OUR BUSINESSAND INDUSTRY
Our business is exposed to supply–demand dynamics in the electronic ceramic material
and component industry and affected by downstream demand for end products in which
our materials and components are used.
We primarily design, develop and manufacture a broad range of electronic and ceramic
materials, electronic components, telecommunication (“telecom”) components, equipment
components and other products. Our products are widely used in telecom, AI and data centers,
consumer electronics, automotive electronics, semiconductor manufacturing and packaging, new
energy and intelligent industrial control applications.Accordingly, our business is closely linked to
the demand for end products in these downstream industries.
Downstream demand for our products is affected by various factors, including (i)
government policies promoting the development of advanced manufacturing, domestic
substitution in semiconductors, renewable energy and smart mobility; (ii) technological
advancements in telecom and AI computing that drive new material and component
requirements; (iii) industrial demand for automation and data infrastructure; and (iv)
macroeconomic conditions affecting industrial investment and infrastructure projects. There is no
assurance that downstream demand will maintain at the same level as during the Track Record
Period or continue to grow in the future. Any downturn, delay or change in these industries’
development may result in reduced orders, slower customer qualifications or lower capacity
utilization for our products. A prolonged decline in downstream demand could lead to
overcapacity, intensified pricing competition and reduced profitability, which may materially and
adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
If we are unable to retain existing customers or attract new customers, our business,
financial condition and results of operations may be adversely affected.
Our business growth depends significantly on maintaining long-term relationships with our
existing customers and developing new customers.
Certain of our customers maintain qualified supplier lists and conduct periodic reviews of
suppliers’ product quality, delivery performance, and technical capabilities. If we fail to
continuously meet our customers’ requirements for qualified suppliers or are unable to satisfy
customers’ evolving procurement standards, we may fail to retain these customers. Customers’
requirements may change due to technological upgrades, product design adjustments, cost
optimization targets or shifts in supply strategy, any of which could lead to a reduction or
termination of purchases from us.

RISK FACTORS
We face intense competition from other domestic and international electronic ceramic
materials and components manufacturers that supply similar or alternative products to
overlapping customer bases. Upon the expiration of existing supply arrangements, we cannot
assure you that our customers will renew their orders with us on comparable terms, or at all. If we
fail to retain our existing customers, expand our customer base or attract new customers
because our products do not meet evolving market requirements, are not competitively priced, or
fall short in reliability or service quality, our revenue and profitability may decline. Such failure
could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Our international strategy and ability to conduct business in various jurisdictions is
subject to uncertainties and risks.
We derive a significant portion of our revenues from our overseas business. We generated
20.3%, 17.9% and 17.4% of our revenues overseas in 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively. We
expect that overseas sales will continue to account for an important portion of our revenue in the
near future. We face certain risks inherent in our overseas business and risks associated with our
efforts to maintain and expand our overseas business.
Moreover, we have established production bases in Chinese Mainland, Germany and
Thailand as of December 31, 2025. As a result, we face numerous risks, including legal,
regulatory, political, economic, and commercial risks associated with manufacturing and
operating in various jurisdictions, any of which could negatively affect our financial performance.
These risks include: (i) legal, regulatory, political, economic and commercial instability and
uncertainty; (ii) lack of familiarity with local culture and operating and market conditions; (iii)
difficulties and costs of recruiting competent employees locally, and managing overseas
operations; (iv) potential failure to achieve the expected returns from investing in production
bases; (v) potential delay in construction plan from third-party service providers; (vi) labor
disputes and work stoppages at our local operations and suppliers; (vii) intra-group transaction
that may be subject to audit or challenge by the relevant tax authorities; (viii) increased costs
associated with maintaining the ability to understand local markets and follow their trends, as
well as develop and maintain an effective local presence; (ix) changes in foreign trade policies
and regulations by the relevant jurisdictions, including those in relation to sanctions, export
controls, and import restrictions, as well in trade barriers such as unfavorable changes in tariffs;
(x) difficulty in obtaining or enforcing intellectual property rights and agreements and collecting
overdue receivables through local legal systems; (xi) foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations
and strict foreign exchange controls; and (xii) other obstacles and risks related to overseas
manufacturing and operations.
Furthermore, we are subject to various evolving laws and regulations in the PRC and other
jurisdictions where we operate, requiring us to obtain and comply with multiple permits, licenses,
and regulatory approvals. Failure to obtain necessary approvals or adapt to evolving regulatory
requirements may adversely impact our operations. Government inspections and regulatory
reviews could also lead to delays or additional compliance costs. There is no assurance that we
will be able to fulfill pre-conditions for necessary approvals or comply with changes in laws and
regulations in a timely manner. Delays in administrative processing or breaching of laws and
regulations related to export and overseas operations could further disrupt our business and
expansion plans, adversely affecting our financial condition and results of operations.
Fluctuations in the prices of raw materials may adversely affect our profitability and
financial condition.
In 2023, 2024 and 2025, our cost of raw materials accounted for approximately 56.0%,
57.9% and 62.3% of our total cost of sales, respectively, and cost of raw materials accounted for
34.7%, 34.2% and 37.4% of our revenues, respectively. See “Financial Information — Principal

macroeconomic conditions, market demand and supply, energy costs, logistics constraints,
payment terms, geopolitical tensions, natural disasters and speculative activities in commodity
markets. According to Frost & Sullivan, alumina is a key raw material for electronic substrates
and packaging due to its excellent insulation, thermal conductivity, and chemical stability. In
2024, production costs increased due to tighter upstream bauxite supply, causing alumina prices
to rise. In 2025, as new alumina capacity came online domestically and internationally, and the
bauxite supply structure gradually improved, the market supply-demand imbalance eased,
leading alumina prices to decline to approximately RMB3.5 per kg. Zirconia is widely used in
electronic ceramic materials and structural components because of its excellent insulation at
room temperature, corrosion resistance, and low thermal conductivity. As global supply chains
gradually recover, some new zirconia capacity comes online, and demand normalizes, prices fell
from peak levels and stabilized at approximately RMB43.0 per kg in 2025.
We cannot assure you that we will always be able to obtain raw materials in sufficient
quantities or at reasonable prices. Significant increases in the prices of key raw materials could
materially raise our production costs.
If we fail to manage or offset increases in cost of raw materials through pricing adjustments,
cost reduction initiatives or process optimization, our gross margin and profitability may be
adversely affected. Any prolonged or material increase in raw material prices could therefore
have a material and adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

During the Track Record Period, sales to customers based in the United States represented

in Thailand. All products manufactured by our production facility in Thailand and exported to the

products from Thailand, effective from August 1, 2025. We cannot guarantee that the U.S. tariff
applicable to our products from Thailand will not increase. Furthermore, the United States has
announced that tariffs of 40% will be imposed on goods that the U.S. Customs and Border

Any failure to make adequate contributions to various employee benefit plans as required

Companies with operations in Chinese Mainland are required to contribute to a number of
social insurance funds, including funds for pension insurance, unemployment insurance, basic
medical insurance, work-related injury insurance, maternity insurance, and housing provident
fund on behalf of employees in Chinese Mainland. According to applicable PRC laws and
regulations, employers must open social insurance registration accounts and housing provident
fund accounts and contribute to social insurance funds and housing provident funds for the
benefits of their employees.
During the Track Record Period, we and our PRC subsidiaries fail to make adequate

times satisfy the government authorities in Chinese Mainland. In the event of any such
non-compliance, we may be required to pay any shortfall in the contribution of social insurance
plans within a prescribed time period and to pay penalties if we fail to do so. In addition to the
above, if we fail to comply with any other relevant labor laws and regulations in Chinese
Mainland, we may be exposed to penalties or be required to compensate employees.
Furthermore, in light of the Supreme People’s Court’s Interpretation (II) on Issues Concerning the
Application of Law in Labor Dispute Cases 《( 最高人民法院關於審理勞動爭議案件適用法律問題的
解釋（二）》), promulgated on July 31, 2025, and effective as of September 1, 2025, if an
employer and an employee agree or the employee undertakes that social insurance contributions
need not be paid, the People’s Court shall deem such agreement or undertaking invalid. Where
an employer fails to pay social insurance contributions in accordance with the law, and the
employee seeks to terminate the labor contract and claims economic compensation from the
employer pursuant to the Labor Contract Law, the People’ s Court shall support such claims, in
which case, the employer remains liable for paying economic compensation to the employee,
notwithstanding any prior agreement to waive social insurance contributions.

Cyclical fluctuations in the electronic ceramic material and component industry may
materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
The electronic ceramic material and component industry, in which we operate, is inherently
cyclical and characterized by alternating periods of growth and contraction driven by global
technology investment cycles, inventory adjustments and macroeconomic conditions. Demand
for our products is closely tied to end markets including consumer electronics, automotive,
industrial automation, and semiconductor manufacturing. These sectors are in turn affected by
factors such as product upgrade cycles, capital expenditure patterns, technological transitions
and changes in consumer or industrial demand. Historically, the industry has experienced
fluctuations driven by both end-market and inventory dynamics. For example, the decline in
global core ceramic electronic component demand in 2022 reflected a slowdown in consumer
electronics following a strong 2021 base, while the reduction in core ceramic telecom component
demand in 2023 was largely due to an industry-wide inventory destocking cycle, which reduced
procurement of communication components such as ceramic ferrules and sleeves.
Against this backdrop, our performance did not solely track the industry upturns. Since the
mild industry downturn in 2023, the sector has generally been in a phase of steady growth rather
than a sharp cyclical upswing. Our revenue growth during this period has been primarily
attributable to market share gains in targeted applications in addition to a broad industry
rebound, supported by deeper penetration in automotive, AI and data center and industrial
control, and by a richer product mix.
If market conditions were to reverse, our exposure to cyclicality would be mitigated by
several structural features of our business. We operate a diversified product and business
portfolio across electronic and ceramic materials, electronic components, telecom components
– 51 –

=== PAGE 61 ===
RISK FACTORS
and equipment components, with exposure to multiple end markets and customer programs,
which reduces reliance on any single segment or cycle. Our qualification base and engagement
in higher-specification applications provide a more resilient demand profile, and our pricing, order
management and production planning practices are designed to adjust run-rates and inventory
levels in response to changing conditions. Nonetheless, an industry-wide downturn or renewed
inventory correction could lead to lower order volumes, less favorable product mix and increased
pricing pressure, which may adversely affect our operating results.
During periods of industry downturn, customers may reduce or defer orders, adjust
inventory levels or postpone capacity expansion, which could result in lower sales volumes and
pricing pressure. Conversely, during periods of strong market demand, we may face challenges
in expanding production capacity, securing sufficient raw materials, or maintaining timely delivery
and quality performance, which could affect our operational efficiency and customer satisfaction.
Cyclical changes in the industry may also require us to adjust our business strategies and
operational plans. In a downturn, we may implement cost-control measures, reduce production or
defer investment projects, which could affect our long-term growth prospects. During upturns,
rapid scaling of production could increase pressure on working capital and expose us to
operational bottlenecks. If we fail to effectively anticipate or manage these cyclical fluctuations,
our business, financial condition and results of operations could be materially and adversely
affected.

On July 14, 2006, the Supreme People’s Court and the Government of the Hong Kong

designated court of China or Hong Kong court has made an enforceable final judgment requiring

payment of money in a civil and commercial case pursuant to a choice of court agreement, the

On January 18, 2019, the Supreme People’s Court and the Department of Justice under the

Reciprocal Recognition and Enforcement of Judgments in Civil and Commercial Matters by the

January 29, 2024. The 2019 Arrangement regulates, among others, the scope and particulars of
judgments, the procedures and methods of the application for recognition or enforcement, the

the recognition and enforcement of a judgment shall be refused and the approaches towards

matters between the courts in China and those in Hong Kong. However, the 2008 Arrangement
will remain applicable to a “choice of court agreement in writing” within the meaning of the 2008

We may be subject to additional regulatory requirements under new laws and regulations

On July 6, 2021, the relevant PRC government authorities issued the Opinions on Strictly
Cracking Down Illegal SecuritiesActivities inAccordance with the Law《( 關於依法從嚴打擊證券違

On February 17, 2023, the CSRC issued the Trial Measures for the Administration on
Overseas Securities Offering and Listing by Domestic Companies 《( 境內企業境外發行證券和上市
管理試行辦法》) and five supporting guidelines, which had become effective on March 31, 2023
(“Overseas Listing Regulations”). The Overseas Listing Regulations are applicable to overseas
securities offering and listing conducted by issuers who are (i) companies incorporated in the
PRC (“PRC domestic companies”) and (ii) companies incorporated overseas with substantial
operations in the PRC. The Overseas Listing Regulations lay out the arrangements for regulatory
filings for both direct and indirect overseas offerings and clarify the determination criteria for
indirect overseas offerings in overseas markets. According to the Overseas Listing Regulations,
we, as a PRC domestic company seeking to offer and list securities in overseas markets, are
required to fulfill the filing procedure with the CSRC within three working days after submitting
the application documents to the overseas supervisory authorities, and we plan to fulfill the
required filing procedures. See “Regulatory Overview — Regulations on Overseas Listings.” If a
domestic company fails to complete the filing procedure or conceals any material fact or falsifies
any major content in its filing documents, such domestic company may be subject to
administrative penalties, such as orders to rectify, warnings, fines, and its controlling
shareholders, actual controllers, the person directly in charge and other directly liable persons
may also be subject to administrative penalties, such as warnings and fines.

RISK FACTORS
Individual holders of H Shares who are not residents of mainland China and whose names
appear on the register of members of H Shares (“non-mainland China resident individual
holders”) are subject to PRC individual income tax on dividends received from us. Pursuant to
the Circular on Questions Concerning the Collection of Individual Income Tax Following the
Repeal of Guo Shui Fa [1993] No. 045 《( 關於國稅發[1993] 045號文件廢止後有關個人所得稅徵管
問題的通知》) (Guo Shui Han [2011] No. 348) (國稅函[2011] 348號), dated June 28, 2011, issued
by the SAT, dividends paid to non-mainland China resident individual holder of H Shares are
generally subject to individual income tax of the PRC at the withholding tax rate of 10.0%,
dependent on whether there is any applicable tax treaty between mainland China and the
jurisdiction in which the non-mainland China resident individual holder of H Shares resides as
well as the tax arrangement between mainland China and Hong Kong. Non-mainland China
resident individual holders who reside in jurisdictions that have not entered into tax treaties with
mainland China are subject to a 20.0% withholding tax on dividends received from us. In
addition, under the Individual Income Tax Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國個人所得稅法》) and
its implementation regulations, non-mainland China resident individual holders of H Shares are
subject to individual income tax at a rate of 20.0% on gains realized upon the sale or other
disposition of H Shares. However, pursuant to the Circular Declaring that Individual Income Tax
Continues to be Exempted over Income of Individuals from Transfer of Shares 《( 關於個人轉讓股
票所得繼續暫免徵收個人所得稅的通知》) issued by the MOF and the SAT on March 30, 1998,
gains of individuals derived from the transfer of listed shares in enterprises may be exempt from
individual income tax. As of the Latest Practicable Date, no aforesaid provisions have expressly
provided that whether individual income tax shall be levied from non-mainland China resident
individual holders on the transfer of shares in mainland China resident enterprises listed on
overseas stock exchanges, and to our knowledge, in practice the mainland China tax authorities
had not collected individual income tax on such gains. If such tax is collected in the future, the
value of such individual holders’ investments in H Shares may be materially and adversely
affected.
Under the Enterprise Income Tax Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國企業所得稅法》) (“EIT
Law”) and its implementation regulations, a non-mainland China resident enterprise is generally
subject to enterprise income tax at a rate of 10.0% with respect to its mainland China-sourced
income, including dividends received from a mainland China company and gains derived from the
disposal of equity interests in a mainland China company, subject to reductions under any special
arrangement or applicable treaty between mainland China and the jurisdiction in which the
non-mainland China resident enterprise resides. The interpretation and implementation of the
EIT Law and its implementation regulations by mainland China tax authorities, including whether
and how enterprise income tax on gains derived upon the sale or other disposal of H Shares will
be collected from non-mainland China resident enterprise holders of H Shares, are to be
determined in accordance with the relevant laws and regulations in effect at the time. If such tax
is collected in the future, the value of such non-mainland China resident enterprise holders’
investments in H Shares may be materially and adversely affected.

remittance.
We receive a majority of payments from our operations in the PRC in RMB and may need to

currency may restrict our ability to remit sufficient foreign currency to pay dividends or other
payments, or otherwise fulfill our foreign currency denominated obligations.

Our A Shares are listed and traded on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, and the
characteristics of theAshare and H share markets may differ.
OurAShares are listed and traded on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange. Following the Global
Offering, our A Shares will continue to be traded on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange and our H
Shares will be traded on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. Under current laws and regulations of
PRC, without the approval from the relevant regulatory authorities, our H Shares and A Shares
are neither interchangeable nor fungible, and there is no trading or settlement between the H
Share and A Share markets. With different trading characteristics, the H Share and A Share
markets have divergent trading volumes, liquidity and investor bases, as well as different levels
of retail and institutional investor participation. As a result, the trading performance of our H
Shares and A Shares may not be comparable. Nonetheless, fluctuations in the price of our A
Shares may adversely affect the price of our H Shares, and vice versa. Due to the different
characteristics of the H Share andAShare markets, the historical prices of ourAShares may not
be indicative of the performance of our H Shares. You should therefore not place undue reliance
on the trading history of ourAShares when evaluating the investment decision in our H Shares.
There has been no prior public market for our H Shares, and an active trading market for
our H Shares may not develop or be sustained.
Prior to the Global Offering, there was no public market for our H Shares. We cannot assure
you that a public market for our H Shares with adequate liquidity and trading volume will develop
and be sustained following the completion of the Global Offering. In addition, the Offer Price of
our H Shares is expected to be fixed by agreement between the Overall Coordinator (for itself

H Shares following the completion of the Global Offering. If an active public market for our H
Shares does not develop following the completion of the Global Offering, the market price and
liquidity of our H Shares may be materially and adversely affected.

WAIVERS FROM STRICT COMPLIANCE WITH THE LISTING RULES
In preparation of the Global Offering, the Company has sought the following waivers from
strict compliance with the relevant provisions of the Listing Rules and the Companies (Winding
Up and Miscellaneous Provisions) Ordinance:
WAIVER IN RESPECT OF MANAGEMENT PRESENCE IN HONG KONG
Rules 8.12 and 19A.15 of the Listing Rules provide that a new applicant for listing on the
Stock Exchange must have a sufficient management presence in Hong Kong and, under normal
circumstances, at least two of the new applicant’s executive directors must be ordinarily resident
in Hong Kong. Rule 19A.15 of the Listing Rules further provides that the requirement in Rule 8.12
of the Listing Rules may be waived by having regard to, among other considerations, the
Company’s arrangements for maintaining regular communication with the Stock Exchange.
The Company’s headquarters are based, and most of the business operations of the Group
are managed in the PRC. The executive Directors ordinarily reside in the PRC, as the Board
believes it would be more effective and efficient for the executive Directors to be based in a
location where the Group’s substantial operations are located. As such, the Company does not
and, in the foreseeable future, will not be able to comply with the requirements of Rules 8.12 and
19A.15 of the Listing Rules for sufficient management presence in Hong Kong.
Accordingly, pursuant to Rule 19A.15 of the Listing Rules, the Company has applied to the
Stock Exchange for, and the Stock Exchange has granted, a waiver from strict compliance with
the requirements under Rules 8.12 and 19A.15 of the Listing Rules, provided that the Company
implements the following arrangements:
(i) the Company has appointed Mr. Li Gang and Ms. Guo Hong (“Ms. Guo”) as the
authorized representatives of the Company (the “Authorized Representatives”) for
the purpose of Rule 3.05 of the Listing Rules. The Authorized Representatives will
serve as the Company’s principal channel of communication with the Stock Exchange.
They can be readily contactable by phone and email to deal promptly with enquiries
from the Stock Exchange and will also be available to meet with the Stock Exchange to
discuss any matters on short notice. The contact details of the Authorized
Representatives have been provided to the Stock Exchange;
(ii) all the Directors who are not ordinarily resident in Hong Kong possess or can apply for
valid travel documents to visit Hong Kong and can meet with the Stock Exchange
within a reasonable period. In addition, each Director has provided his/her contact
details, including office phone numbers, mobile phone numbers, email addresses and
fax numbers (if any), to theAuthorized Representatives and to the Stock Exchange, so
that each of theAuthorized Representatives and the Stock Exchange would be able to
contact all the Directors (including the independent non-executive Directors) promptly
at all times if and when the Stock Exchange wishes to contact the Directors;
(iii) the Company has appointed Somerley Capital Limited as its Compliance Advisor for
the period commencing on the Listing Date and ending on the date on which the
Company complies with Rule 13.46 of the Listing Rules in respect of the Company’s
financial results for the first full financial year commencing after the Listing Date, or
until the agreement is terminated, whichever is earlier. The ComplianceAdvisor will act
as the Company’s additional and alternative channel of communication with the Stock
Exchange, and its representatives will be readily available to answer enquiries from
the Stock Exchange; and

DISCLOSURE OF OFFER PRICE
Paragraph 15(2)(c) of Appendix D1A to the Listing Rules provides that the issue price or
offer price of each security must be disclosed in the prospectus. Pursuant to Paragraph 12 of
Chapter 4.14 of the Listing Guide, the Stock Exchange also allows an indicative offer price range
to be included in the prospectus, as an alternative to the disclosure of a fixed offer price.
We have applied to the Stock Exchange a waiver from strict compliance with paragraph
15(2)(c) of Appendix D1A to the Listing Rules so that the Company will only disclose the
maximum Offer Price in this prospectus on the below basis:
(a) the Offer Price will be determined with reference to, among other factors, the closing
price of the Company’sAShares on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange on the last trading
day on or before the Price Determination Date. Our Company is unable to control the
trading price of ourAShares on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange;
(b) setting a fixed offer price or an offer price range with a low-end may adversely affect
(a) the market price of our A Shares, (b) our ability to price the Offer Shares given
potential price fluctuations of our A Shares during the period from the date of this
prospectus until the pricing of the Global Offering; and (c) our ability to price our H
Shares in the best interests of our Shareholders and the market price of the A Shares
and the Hong Kong Offer Shares;

CONSENT IN RESPECT OF CORNERSTONE INVESTMENT BY CONNECTED CLIENTS
Paragraph 1C(1) of Appendix F1 to the Listing Rules provides that no allocations will be
permitted to “connected clients” of the overall coordinator(s), any syndicate member(s) (other
than the overall coordinator(s)) or any distributor(s) (other than syndicate member(s)), without
the prior written consent of the Stock Exchange.
Chapter 4.15 of the Guide for New Listing Applicants provides that the Stock Exchange will
ordinarily give its consent for allocation to connected clients if it is satisfied that: (i) the allocation
to a connected client represents genuine demand for securities of an applicant; and (ii) the
connected client has not taken and will not take advantage of its position to receive an allocation
for its own benefit at the expense of other placees or the public (i.e. no actual or perceived
preferential treatment has been given to such connected client).

OVERVIEW OF GLOBAL ELECTRONIC CERAMIC MATERIALAND COMPONENT INDUSTRY
Definition and Classification
Advanced ceramics, also known as special ceramics, fine ceramics, high-performance
ceramics, or high-tech ceramics, are a category of new high-end ceramic materials
fundamentally different from traditional construction or daily-use ceramics in terms of raw
material selection, formulation design, and processing technologies. These materials typically
use high-purity, ultrafine ceramic powders as core raw materials and are manufactured through
precise chemical stoichiometry, customized composition and structural design, and a
combination of precision forming, high-temperature sintering, and other advanced composite
processes. They exhibit excellent mechanical strength, insulation, thermal conductivity,
high-temperature resistance, corrosion resistance, dimensional stability, and biocompatibility,
enabling reliable and long-lifetime performance across multiple high-reliability application fields.
As the high-end and core category within ceramic materials, advanced ceramics serve as
essential foundational materials for key sectors of the national economy, such as telecoms, AI
and data centers, consumer electronics, automotive electronics, semiconductor manufacturing
and packaging, new energy, and intelligent industrial control. Compared with traditional ceramics,
their core advantages stem from higher raw-material purity, more precise processing, and stricter
machining control. These advantages allow them to support miniaturization of electronic
components, efficiency improvements in new-energy devices, and precision requirements in
semiconductor manufacturing, making advanced ceramics an indispensable pillar of the modern
electronics and high-end manufacturing ecosystem.
Electronic ceramic materials and components are functional or structural key parts derived
from advanced ceramics through precision machining and sintering. They are widely used in the
high-tech industries mentioned above. Core product categories include electronic ceramic
materials, ceramic electronic components, ceramic telecom components, ceramic equipment
components, and others. Together they form a complete product system extending from
foundational materials to end-application components, providing essential support for the global
high-end manufacturing sector.

Drivers and Development Trends Analysis of Global Electronic Ceramic Material and
Component Industry
Booming Demand in Key Downstream Sectors Drives Continuous Industry Expansion
The electronic ceramic material and component industry is currently in a high-growth phase,
driven by the synchronous upgrading of key sectors of the national economy, including telecoms,
AI and data centers, consumer electronics, automotive electronics, semiconductor manufacturing
and packaging, new energy, and intelligent industrial control. Trends such as premiumization in
consumer electronics, widespread adoption of AI and IoT, electrification and intelligence of
vehicles, global expansion of computing infrastructure, deepening domestic substitution in
semiconductors, and the energy transition collectively boost demand across all product
categories, continuously expanding industry scale.
• Telecoms: By 2030, the number of global 5G/6G base stations is expected to reach
over 20 million units. The large-scale deployment of 5G/6G base stations and the
upgrade toward gigabit broadband have raised the requirements for signal
transmission stability and high-speed interconnection, driving growth in ceramic
ferrules and sleeves as well as high-capacitance MLCCs. Simultaneously, upgrades in
high-speed optical communication networks have driven a simultaneous increase in
demand for MT ferrules and MT short jumpers, and optical communication ceramic
packages;
• AI and Data Centers: Global data center capital expenditure reached over USD500
billion in 2025, and is expected to increase to over USD3 trillion by 2030. As AI data
centers evolve towards larger scale and higher power density, the power density per
rack has increased from under 10kW to over 120kW. Higher power density in
computing equipment presents challenges for heat dissipation and power supply,
significantly increasing demand for high-capacitance, high-reliability MLCCs and
high-thermal-conductivity ceramic substrates. Massive data transmission drives
adoption of high-speed optical modules, further expanding demand for ceramic
telecom components;
• Consumer Electronics: Driven by the integration of innovative products and the
accelerated adoption of AI applications, global shipments of consumer electronics
products are projected to increase from 2.2 billion units in 2025 to reach approximately
2.7 billion units by 2030. Devices are increasingly miniaturized, lightweight, and
multifunctional, raising requirements for miniaturized and reliable electronic
– 81 –

=== PAGE 91 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
components. Demand for small-size high-capacitance MLCCs, miniaturized PKGs, and
alumina ceramic substrates continues to grow. Different types of ceramic electronic
components will form a synergistic supply to meet one-stop procurement needs;
• Automotive Electronics: It is expected that global sales volume of NEVs will increase
from nearly 24 million units in 2025 to over 40 million units by 2030. Under the trends
of electrification, intelligence, and connectivity, both the quantity and performance
requirements of electronic components in vehicles and on-board equipment are rising.
MLCCs and PKGs in NEVs are used in significantly higher volumes than in
conventional vehicles. To ensure stable operation of more on-board systems, demand
for ceramic substrates and pan-semiconductor ceramic components will further
increase;
• Semiconductor Manufacturing and Packaging: Accelerating domestic substitution
drives increasing demand for high-purity, high-precision ceramic components;
• New Energy: The clean energy transition drives SOFC adoption in distributed power
and energy storage scenarios, boosting demand for SOFC electrolyte sheets and other
relevant components. Meanwhile, rising heat dissipation and power regulation
requirements from NEVs and energy storage devices expand demand for
high-performance ceramic substrates and high-capacitance MLCCs;
• Intelligent Industrial Control: Automation and high-end transformation drive expanded
applications of industrial robots, and intelligent sensors. High-voltage MLCCs and
alumina ceramic substrates for these applications continue to see strong demand.
High-precision piezo microdispensing systems and pan-semiconductor ceramic
components also expand.
Stringent Requirements in High-End Scenarios Drive Continuous Material Performance
Upgrades
Electronic ceramic materials and components are continuously upgrading along the path of
“functional precision matching + performance boundary breakthroughs” to meet the global
high-end manufacturing demand for high performance, high reliability, and high adaptability. The
core evolution of material systems stems from the synergistic optimization of high-purity ceramic
powders, electronic pastes, and specialized functional ceramics. For instance, alumina enhances
insulation and structural stability through increased purity; electronic pastes support miniaturized
component preparation by upgrading conductivity and printing precision; while SOFC ceramic
materials achieve a balance between hermeticity and ion conduction efficiency through
formulation optimization. Simultaneously, focusing on three key directions: resistance to extreme
environments, low impurity interference, and high functional stability, the industry is achieving
full-chain performance enhancements through powder modification, microstructure control, and
formulation upgrades. This propels the ceramic materials system from “import substitution”
toward “performance leadership,” further enhancing the reliability, energy conversion efficiency,
and useful life of end-use systems.
Product Functional Integration Meets Compact Design and ScenarioAdaptation
As end-user devices increasingly demand high-density integration, system stability, and
lightweight design, the electronic ceramics materials and components industry is accelerating
toward functional integration. Through the coordinated optimization of material systems and
device structures, multiple functions are being realized within more compact dimensions. From a
product functionality perspective, core industry products are increasingly breaking through
single-function limitations and upgrading toward multi-feature integration to meet downstream
device requirements. For example, MLCCs achieve miniaturization while further integrating high
capacitance and high-voltage tolerance, combining filtering and voltage-stabilizing functions to
support compact circuit designs in consumer electronics and automotive applications. Ceramic
structural components have expanded from purely structural support to include insulation, heat
– 82 –

=== PAGE 92 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
dissipation, and corrosion resistance. Ceramic substrates, in addition to basic insulation, further
integrate high thermal conductivity to support both heat dissipation and circuit stability for
high-power devices.
Accelerated Domestic Substitution, Expanding Market Share for Domestic Companies
The domestic substitution of electronic ceramic materials and components is accelerating
globally, becoming one of the key forces reshaping the industry landscape. Policy support is the
primary driver. Advanced ceramics have been designated as strategic materials in many
countries. In China, for example, the “14th Five-Year Plan for National Economic and Social
Development and the 2035 Long-Term Goals” emphasizes promoting breakthroughs in
high-performance ceramics and other advanced new materials; the “14th Five-Year Plan for the
Development of the Raw Materials Industry” lists advanced ceramic powder technology as a key
area for technological innovation; and the “Suggestions of the CPC Central Committee on
Formulating the 15th Five-Year Plan for National Economic and Social Development” explicitly
calls for strengthening core technology R&D in advanced materials.
Meanwhile, the rapid expansion of China’s downstream industries, including new energy
vehicles, 5G communications, and semiconductor manufacturing, has created vast domestic
application scenarios for electronic ceramic materials, offering domestic manufacturers iterative
opportunities to “drive research through application.” Domestic enterprises will accelerate
breakthroughs in multiple fields, such as ceramic substrates, high-end electronic pastes, MLCCs,
and ceramic telecom components. In addition, domestic substitution is extending from end
products to core raw materials and key processes, gradually forming a self-reliant and
controllable full-chain system. Supported by cost advantages and localized service capabilities,
domestic enterprises are continuously increasing their penetration in high-end markets such as
automotive and semiconductor packaging, while accelerating overseas expansion. Domestic
substitution is evolving from “single-point breakthroughs” to “system-wide replacement,” further
shifting the global competitiveness focus towards China.
Coordination of Materials and Processes Drives Integration
As the industry’s requirements for product performance, miniaturization, and reliability
continue to rise, companies are actively promoting integration across materials and processes.
By optimizing these three dimensions (product performance, miniaturization, and reliability) in a
coordinated manner, companies can rapidly respond to downstream product iteration needs,
improve yield, and achieve performance breakthroughs.At the materials stage, precise control of
core materials such as high-purity ceramic powders and electronic pastes helps reduce
production variability and material waste. At the process stage, meticulous management of
critical steps such as tape casting and sintering enables highly consistent and reliable product
output. Overall, this integration not only accelerates technical responsiveness and yield
improvement but also delivers cost advantages through coordinated operations, serving as a key
driver for enhancing competitive strength.
Global Operations and Regional Adaptation Optimize Market Coverage and Cost
Structures
Companies adopt a “global layout, regional adaptation” strategy to approach target markets,
reduce regional costs, and mitigate trade risks. Production bases are established in domestic
industrial clusters, with overseas manufacturing hubs meeting local market needs. Local
technical service teams in key overseas markets shorten response times, while international
certifications ensure compliance. Combining global operations with regional adaptation optimizes
costs and enhances market penetration.

Definition and Classification
Electronic ceramic materials refer to functional material products used in the manufacturing
of electronic components, featuring excellent dielectric, conductive, thermal, insulating, and
structural support properties. These ceramic materials possess a variety of functional

substrates for electronic components, modules, and system packaging, with broad applications in
electronic information, automotive electronics, optical communications, new energy, and
low-altitude economy sectors. They form the foundational basis for the development of high-end
electronic manufacturing.
Market Size of Global Core Electronic Ceramic Material Industry
The core driver of global core electronic ceramic material market growth comes from the
continuous expansion of downstream electronic product demand, iterative demand in new energy

electronics, new energy, and high-end consumer electronics. Additionally, the rapid growth of

expanding application opportunities for electronic ceramic materials.

Drivers and Development Trends Analysis of Global Core Electronic Ceramic Material
Industry
High-Power Electronics and Smart Manufacturing Drive Upgrading of Ceramic Substrates
With the rapid development of NEVs, energy storage systems, industrial automation
equipment, and consumer electronics, downstream applications are placing increasing demands
on the power density and thermal performance of electronic packaging materials, driving growth
in ceramic substrate demand. High-performance ceramics such as ZTA, aluminum nitride and
silicon nitride, with excellent insulation, thermal conductivity, and mechanical strength, have
become key supporting materials for power devices, chip components, and other critical parts,
widely suited for high-power operations and miniaturized designs. At the same time, ceramic
substrates are evolving toward higher thermal efficiency, lower thermal resistance, and stronger
environmental adaptability, better meeting the stringent reliability requirements of high-end
manufacturing scenarios and shifting the electronic ceramic materials market toward higher
value-added segments.
High-End Packaging Innovation Drives Electronic Paste Technology Upgrades
Electronic paste is a key functional material in the manufacturing of ceramic components.
With chip packaging moving toward miniaturization, high frequency, and high-density integration,
traditional electronic paste systems struggle to meet advanced manufacturing requirements.
Electronic pastes are upgrading toward higher thermal conductivity, enhanced heat resistance,
greater stability, and environmental friendliness, while optimizing process compatibility with new
ceramic substrate materials. In addition, technological breakthroughs by domestic manufacturers
in paste formulation and particle dispersion control are accelerating the domestic substitution of
– 85 –

=== PAGE 95 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
certain niche products. Looking ahead, with the widespread adoption of advanced packaging
technologies such as 3D packaging and system-in-package (SiP), the demand for
high-performance electronic pastes is expected to grow further, serving as a core material
support for high-end electronic manufacturing.
Expansion of High-Energy-Consumption Scenarios and Carbon Neutrality Goals Drive
SOFC Electrolyte Sheet Demand
High-energy-consumption scenarios such as data centers and AI computing clusters are
accelerating deployment, posing supply shortages to traditional power systems. SOFCs, with
high energy conversion efficiency, low carbon emissions, and fuel flexibility, have emerged as a
key distributed power solution. As a core functional component of SOFCs, the performance of
SOFC electrolyte sheets directly affects system efficiency and lifespan, and demand for these
plates is expected to grow alongside SOFC commercialization. Against the backdrop of global
carbon neutrality goals and ongoing expansion of computing infrastructure, the application scale
of SOFCs will continue to expand. At the same time, SOFC electrolyte sheet technology is
expected to iterate toward higher performance, greater reliability, and lower cost.
OVERVIEW OF GLOBAL CORE CERAMIC ELECTRONIC COMPONENT INDUSTRY
Definition and Classification
Ceramic electronic components are passive electronic devices that use ceramic materials
as the primary dielectric or substrate, leveraging their superior dielectric, piezoelectric,
thermal-stability and insulation properties to store, conduct, convert or filter electrical energy.
They are widely used in consumer electronics, communication devices, automotive electronics,
industrial control and new energy areas, and are indispensable basic components in the
electronic-information industry.
Market Size of Global Core Ceramic Electronic Component Industry
The development of the electronics manufacturing industry has driven rising demand for
core ceramic electronic components. From 2021 to 2025, the global market size of core ceramic
electronic components increased from RMB162.2 billion to RMB182.1 billion, representing a
CAGR of 2.9%. The decline in global core ceramic electronic component market size in 2022 was
mainly driven by geopolitical tensions, which disrupted supply chains, heightened
macroeconomic uncertainty, constrained global economic recovery, and led to a downturn in
consumer electronics demand after a high 2021 base, despite continued growth in emerging
applications such as automotive electronics. For example, the global shipments of consumer
electronics products decreased by 7.8% in 2022. China has emerged as a key manufacturing and
demand hub, supported by its comprehensive electronics ecosystem and broad downstream
applications, and continues to play a central role in driving market growth and industry upgrading.
