=== PAGE 123 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
These export controls are enforced on national EU member state level, in Germany via the
German Foreign Trade and Payments Act (Außenwirtschaftsgesetz (AWG)) and the German
Ordinance on Foreign Trade and Payments (Außenwirtschaftsverordnung (AWV)). These laws
establish the applicable national procedures, additional controls, and penalties in case of
violations for the implementation of dual-use and military item controls as well as EU sanctions.
The Federal Office for Economic Affairs and Export Control (BAFA) is Germany’s central
export licensing authority. BAFA is responsible for examining export license applications in light
of Germany’s security and foreign policy interests, particularly the prevention of proliferation and
the destabilizing accumulation of advanced military technology. Further authorities with
competences in the implementation of foreign trade law in Germany include customs offices,
Deutsche Bundesbank and the Public Prosecutor’s Office.
Employee Health and Safety
German law establishes a system of rules and regulations to protect employees’ health and
safety at work. German occupational safety regulation is largely shaped by the requirements of
EU law which contains numerous regulations regarding different aspects of technical and social
health and safety at work. In particular, general obligations on employers, protective and
preventive services, emergency measures and necessary information, as well as the
consultation, participation and training of workers are laid out in the Council Directive
89/391/EEC on the introduction of measures to encourage improvements in the safety and health
of workers at work. EU Member States are free to maintain or establish more stringent measures
of protection than those provided by Directive 89/391/EEC.
In Germany, significant occupational safety provisions are contained in the German Act on
the Implementation of Measures of Occupational Safety and Health to Encourage Improvements
in the Safety and Health Protection of Workers at Work (Arbeitsschutzgesetz (ArbSchG)) and in
the German Act on Occupational Physicians, Safety Engineers and Other Occupational Safety
Specialists (Arbeitssicherheitsgesetz), which require employers to ensure safety of their
employees.TheArbSchG sets out the fundamental duties of employers and employees regarding
health protection. It places employers under an obligation to assess the hazards of the workplace
and to take the appropriate preventive measures, as well as to instruct employees about these
measures. Employers must take precautions for especially hazardous workplaces and situations.
They must also provide preventive occupational healthcare.
In regulatory supervision, German law enforcement authorities have wide-ranging
enforcement powers, including the right to enter a company’s premises, search for documents
and examine the work equipment and the personal health equipment.They are also authorized to
impose fines.
Laws Governing Employee’s Inventions
German law provides for special rules governing intellectual property protection in the
relation between employer and employee due to the fact that the majority of creative works is
developed in the course of employment. Generally, an employer provides for the means enabling
employees to come up with intellectual ideas in the course of employment. The German
Employee’s Invention Act (Arbeitnehmererfindungsgesetz) basically sets out that under the
aforementioned circumstances intellectual property rights rest with the employer while the
employee is entitled to appropriate compensation.
– 114 –

=== PAGE 124 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
In relation to software, German copyright law provides for an overriding rule for software
developed by employees. Under Section 69b of the German CopyrightAct (Urheberrechtsgesetz)
copyrights vest in the employer by operation of law. In special employment situations, such as in
case of freelancing, the parties’ will regarding the allocation of property rights must be expressly
agreed upon.
The infringement of copyrights can result in a variety of sanctions, including preliminary
injunctions or damages.
Foreign Investment Regime
Under Germany’s foreign investment regime, set out in the AWG and the AWV, direct and
indirect acquisitions of stakes in German companies may be subject to screening and, in certain
cases, mandatory notification. A mandatory notification may be required for acquisitions as low
as acquisitions of not less than 10% of the voting rights in listed, highly sensitive sectors like
defense, critical infrastructure, healthcare, or advanced technologies, with subsequent reviews at
20%, 25%, 40%, 50%, or 75%. The activity of the German target company is decisive for the
applicable voting right threshold and which foreign investors trigger a review (non-EU/EFTA or
non-German). In non-listed sectors, acquisitions of not less than 25% of the voting rights by
non-EU/EFTAinvestors are only subject to a discretionary call-in regime for a max. 5-year period.
Certain share acquisition conferring “atypical control” to the foreign investor via additional rights,
can trigger the regime and, in certain sectors, require mandatory notification. If notification is
mandatory and pending clearance, certain standstill obligations apply, and the transaction is
invalid; infringements are subject to penalties. Special rules apply to stock exchange securities
transactions. The regime has tightened since 2018, with over 300 cases reviewed in 2024,
focusing on energy, tech, and healthcare.
The Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy (BMWE) conducts reviews, with
Phase 1 (two months) and Phase 2 (up to four months; subject to further extensions and
suspensions). It may prohibit or restrict the acquisition by a foreign investor on grounds of public
order or security or clear the transaction.
Data Protection
The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR, 2016/679/EU) is a uniform framework
laying down principles and rules for data processing. Many EU member states have enacted
national implementation acts which accompany the directly applicable GDPR, such as the
German Federal Data Protection Act (Bundesdatenschutzgesetz (BDSG)). The GDPR and the
BDSG entail strict requirements, obligations and restrictions for the collection, storage, transfer,
and further processing of personal data, in particular (without limitation) for lawful processing,
transparency, international data transfers, storage limitation, data mapping and accountability,
processor (service provider) obligations, joint controllership, notification of data breaches and the
requirement to designate a data protection officer and/or EU representative, as applicable. Under
the GDPR, the regulatory requirements include that personal data: (i) may only be collected for
specified, explicit and legitimate purposes based on a legal ground set out in the GDPR or in
national laws; (ii) may only be further processed in a manner consistent with those purposes; (iii)
must also be adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary in relation to the purposes for
which it is processed; (iv) must be processed in a manner that ensures transparency, fairness
and appropriate security of the personal data; and (v) must not be transferred outside of the
European Union unless certain steps are taken to ensure an adequate level of protection and
must not be kept for longer than necessary for the purposes of collection or further processing.
Data subjects, i.e., an identified or identifiable natural person to whom the personal data relates,
have far-reaching rights in relation to the processing of their personal data, such as the right to
access, rectification, deletion, restriction of processing and data portability. The GDPR sets out
substantial fines for violations of the data protection rules and other administrative sanctions.

REGULATORY OVERVIEW
These sanctions range from formal warnings and cease-and-desist orders to fines of up to €20
million or up to 4% of the total worldwide annual turnover of the offending data processor in the
preceding fiscal year, whichever is higher, for each infraction.
REGULATORY ENVIRONMENT — THAILAND
Through our Thai subsidiary, Glory Winner, headquartered in Thailand, we operate in
Thailand as a developer and manufacturer of ceramic products.
Civil and Commercial Code of Thailand (“CCC”)
Laws governing the formation and incorporation of types of Thai business entities can be
found in the Civil and Commercial Code of Thailand (“CCC”).Aprivate limited company is formed
through a process which leads to the registration of a Memorandum ofAssociation andArticles of
Association (By-laws), as its constitutive documents. A company is formed with the registered
capital and divided into shares to be subscribed by the promoters or shareholders. The liability of
the shareholders is limited to the amount unpaid on the shares respectively held by them.
Incorporation and Promoters
There must be a minimum of 3 (three) promoters for a private limited company who are
responsible for subscribing and registering the incorporation of the company with the DBD as it is
stated in Section 1097 of the CCC that any three or more persons may promote and form a
limited company by subscribing their names to a memorandum and otherwise complying with the
provisions of the CCC. The promoters must be individual persons (not juristic entities). The
promoters can be foreigners and/or Thai nationals. However, each promoter is required to be
among the company’s initial shareholders immediately upon the company’s registration and is
required to subscribe and hold a minimum of one share upon the company’s registration. They
are generally free to transfer those shares to existing shareholders or third parties, thereafter, if
they wish. However, the number of shareholders in a company shall always remain not less than
3 (three) shareholders (individual and/or juristic entities) as required by the CCC.
Noted that after 7 February 2023, the requirement of minimum shareholders of 3 persons is
reduced to 2 persons according to Section 1097 of CCC.
Memorandum ofAssociation (“MOA”)
The Memorandum of Association of the company has to be filed with the DBD and must
include the name of the company that has been successfully reserved and approved by the DBD,
the physical address where the company will be located in Thailand, its business objectives, the
capital to be registered, and the names of the promoters.
Articles ofAssociation (“AOA”)
TheArticles ofAssociation are the regulations of the company concerning its internal affairs
such as shares, general meetings, voting rights, directors and auditors, distribution of dividends,
dissolution etc. It is one of the most important corporate documents, the content of which is
determined and approved by the statutory meeting or the general meeting of shareholders with a
special resolution (if later amended). A company may choose to either adopt its own Articles of
Association or refer to the relevant provisions of the CCC.
Registered Capital
In general, the registered amount of the capital should be respectable enough and adequate
for the intended business operation. The registered capital will be divided into shares with the
same par value, which must not be less than THB 5 (Five Thai Baht) per share. All shares must
– 116 –

=== PAGE 126 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
be subscribed, and at least 25% (twenty-five percent) of the subscribed shares must be paid up.
If the company intends to employ foreigners, the minimum registered capital requirements for
applying work permit may also apply. The company must have registered capital of not less than
THB 2 Million (two million Thai Baht) with fully paid-up capital for each 1 (one) foreign employee,
or THB 4 Million (four million Thai Baht) share capital for 2 (two) foreign employees, or THB 6
Million (six million Thai Baht) for 3 (three) foreign employees respectively.
Directors
A company shall be managed by at least 1 (one) individual director under the control of the
general meeting of shareholders. There are currently no general restrictions on the nationality of
directors who control a Thai private limited company in Thailand. Therefore, a foreigner can be a
sole director of the company. By law, foreign directors and Thai directors are not treated
differently. However, foreign directors need a work permit to work in Thailand in order to manage
a company by all lawful means necessary within the scope stipulated in the Memorandum of
Association, Articles of Association, the resolutions of shareholders’ meetings, and applicable
Thai laws. Thus, foreign directors residing abroad should pay attention and apply for a work
permit to work inThailand even if they only intend to attend a meeting or training. UnderThai law,
it specifies only the requirements of director and the board of directors for companies (without
having supervisor or board of supervisors). Therefore, a company in Thailand is not required to
have supervisor or board of supervisors which is subject to each company’s management policy
and organization chart.
Shareholders and Shareholders Meeting
Every company is required to hold the annual general meeting (“AGM”) annually. The
extra-general meeting (“EGM”) shall be held upon being called by the directors or one-fifth of the
shareholders.
Notice of every general meeting of shareholders shall be published at least once in a local
paper and be sent to every shareholder of the company by receipt acknowledge registered mail
at least seven (7) days before the date of meeting unless, in case of the general meeting which
has to provide a special resolution, the notice shall be published in a local newspaper and be
sent to every shareholder of the company at least fourteen (14) days before the date of the
meeting.
Shareholders representing not less than 25% of the capital of the company must present at
the shareholders’ meeting to constitute a quorum. A resolution shall be made by a majority vote;
in the case of a tied vote, the Chairman of the meeting shall be entitled to a casting vote.
According to the CCC, a supermajority vote of 75% of total shares is required for passing a
special resolution as required by law, i.e. amendment to the memorandum of association and
articles of association, increase or decrease of registered capital, dissolution, conversion to a
public company and subscription of shares by payment in kind.
In addition, pursuant to Section 1171 of the CCC, the AGM shall be held within 6 months
after the registration and subsequently be held every 12 months.
Share Transfer
Under the CCC, the transfer of shares must be made in writing and signed by the transferor
and transferee whose signatures are certified by at least one witness (the “Share Transfer
Instrument”); otherwise, such transfer shall be void.The ShareTransfer Instrument must contain
at least (i) the name of the transferor and transferee, and (ii) the numbers of the transferred
– 117 –

=== PAGE 127 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
shares. The transfer of shares will become valid against the company and/or any third party only
upon its registration in the share register book specifying the details of the transfer and the name
and address of the transferee.
Share Registered Book
Acompany is required to prepare and keep a share registered book recording the history of
change of shareholders. It is important to note that any share transfers shall be invalid against a
company and third parties until such transfer is recorded in the share registered book. Share
registered book is presumed to be correct evidence of any matters directed or authorized by the
laws.
Under the CCC, in case a company fails to keep a share registered book in accordance with
Section 1138 and fails to have the share registered book opened for inspection by shareholders
upon their request in accordance with Section 1139, the Target Company shall be liable to a fine
not exceeding THB 20,000 under Section 10 and 11 of the Corporate CriminalAct.
Share Certificate
Share certificates shall be issued and delivered by a limited company to each shareholder
for the share held by him. Share certificates shall be signed by at least one of the directors and
affixed with the limited company’s seal; moreover, the share certificate must contain the name of
the company, share number(s), the value of each share and if the shares have not been fully paid
up, the paid amount of each share shall be indicated therein.
Failure to provide share certificates for the shareholders containing the particulars as
specified in Section 1127 and Section 1128 would result in a fine not exceeding THB 10,000
pursuant to Section 8 of the Corporate CriminalAct.
Foreign BusinessAct
Thai law imposes restrictions on foreigners engaging in certain business activities. The
principal law with respect to foreign participation in various business activities is the Foreign
Business Act (the “FBA”). Under the FBA, a “foreigner” is defined as (i) a non-Thai natural
person, (ii) a legal entity not incorporated inThailand, (iii) a juristic entity incorporated inThailand
where at least 50% (fifty percent) of share capital owned by foreign individuals or entities, and
(iv) a limited partnership or a registered ordinary partnership where the managing partner or
manager is a non-Thai natural person. Based on the aforesaid definition, a private limited
company which is owned by majority Thai nationals and/or entities with at least half of the share
capital shall be considered as a Thai private limited company and is not subject to the FBA.
Foreigners therefore are generally allowed to participate and own less than 50% of shares capital
unless otherwise particularly prescribed in specific law, in case the Company intends to engage
in any restricted businesses.
BOIAct
The Thailand Board of Investment (the “BOI”) was set up under the Investment Promotion
Act (the “Investment Act”) for purpose of encouraging investment in Thailand through several
eligible business activities under the BOI promotion. Under the Investment Act, the Thai
government has granted full foreign ownership rights to foreign nationals who promised to make
major investments and transfer technology to Thailand. Generally, the BOI privileges are granted
for manufacturing activities as well as certain non-manufacturing activities that fall within the
eligible activities as listed by the BOI. However, to qualify for the BOI privileges, the foreign
nationals are obligated to transfer into Thailand the specified capital, technology and equipment
technology within the period as set forth in its investment promotion certificate, and strictly
comply with the specific condition as set forth in the investment promotion certificate.

=== PAGE 128 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
Land Code
The Land Code stipulates that foreigners may acquire land by virtue of the provisions of a
treaty giving the right to own immovable property, subject to the provisions of the Land Code and,
subject to the limitation on rights over land for religious purposes, foreigners may acquire land for
residence, commerce, industry, agriculture, burial, public charity or religion under the conditions
and procedures prescribed in ministerial regulations and with the permission of the minister.
Social SecurityAct
The Social SecurityAct of B.E. 2533 (1990) (the “Social Security Act”) in Thailand, and its
amendments, established the Social Security Fund (the “Fund”) with the objective of providing
coverage for fund members under certain conditions.
The stipulations of the Social Security Act apply to every company having one or more
employees. Persons insured under the provisions of the Fund include all employees from the age
of 15 years up through those not over 60 years.
A company having one or more employees must register with the Social Security Office
(“SSO”) for the Fund within 30 days after hiring the first employee. If the company increases the
number of employees, it must submit a new employee registration form for each new employee.
Workmen Compensation Fund
The Workmen’s Compensation Fund was established under the Workmen’s Compensation
Act, B.E. 2537 (1994) (“WCA”) to ensure that adequate compensation is paid when workers are
injured, become ill, or die as a result of their work, or as a result of illnesses arising out of the
nature or conditions of the work, or as the Department of the Interior may prescribe. This
objective will be achieved by requiring employers to register with and contribute to the
Workmen’s Compensation Fund and by having the Department of Labour Protection and Social
Welfare pay the above compensation that employers are required to pay under the Occupational
Safety and HealthAct instead of employees. The contribution rate should be 0.2% – 1%.
Labor ProtectionAct
The Thailand Labour Protection Act (“LPA”) is a comprehensive law that sets out the rights
and obligations of employers and employees in the workplace. It aims to protect the welfare of
workers and ensure fair treatment.
Under section 108 of the Labour Protection Act, B.E. 2535 (1992) (“LPA”), the Target
Company shall formulate and implement the work rules in Thai language upon the date the
employer employed more than ten (10) employees and shall disclose such work rules at the
working place of the employee.As from 4April 2017, the work rules are not required to submit to
the Labour Department in accordance with the Order of the Head of the National Council for
Peace and Order No. 21/2017 dated 4 April 2017 Governing Amendment of Laws for Ease of
Doing Business.
Foreigners’Working Management Emergency Decree
Pursuant to Section 8 of the Foreigners’ Working Management Emergency Decree B.E.
2560 (2017), a foreigner shall not carry out any work prescribed in the Notification issued under
section 7 paragraph one or carry out any work without a work permit.
The Revenue Code
The principal law with respect to tax implication in Thailand is the Revenue Code of
Thailand (the “RC”) governed by the Revenue Department.

REGULATORY OVERVIEW
Corporate Income Tax (“CIT”)
According to the RC, in general, a company is subject to the CIT rate of 20 % on net profit.
In addition, with respect to Small Medium Enterprises (SMEs) which a company has its paid-up
registered capital at the end of the accounting period of not exceeding THB 5 Million and having
annual revenue from business operation not exceeding THB 30 Million per annum shall be
entitled to reduction of CIT in which it will be exempted from CIT for the net profit not over THB
300,000, and it will be subject to 15% CIT on net profit ranging from THB 300,001 – 3,000,000,
and 20% CIT on net profit exceeding THB 3,000,000.
ValueAdded Tax (“VAT”)
VAT is an indirect consumption tax levied on the supply of goods and provision of services
by a VAToperator and on the import of goods or services.Any person (individual or juristic entity)
who conducts business inThailand and its annual turnover exceedsTHB 1.8 Million is required to
register to be a VAToperator.AVAToperator is required to comply with VATrequirements per the
Revenue Code. Only a registered VAT operator is entitled to claim for prepaid VAT credit or VAT
refund.
There are also other applicable taxes, for example, the excise tax, withholding tax, special
business tax, land and building tax and stamp duty, etc.Acompany is required to file tax returns
to the Revenue Department on a regular basis, including monthly, annual and semi-annual
reports.

HISTORY AND CORPORATE STRUCTURE
OVERVIEW
The history of the Company can be traced back to the 1970s when the predecessor of the
Company was founded. The Company was later established as a joint stock company in
December 1992 as a result of the restructuring of the former Chaozhou Radio Ceramic Parts
Factory (潮州市無線電瓷件廠). In December 2014, the A Shares of the Company were listed on
the ChiNext of the Shenzhen Stock Exchange under the stock code 300408.SZ.
The Company has focused on electronic ceramic materials and components for over
fifty-five years. Consistently centered on our core business in ceramic materials, the company
has grown into a company in electronic ceramic materials and components, according to Frost &
Sullivan.

OVERVIEW
Who WeAre
We focus on electronic ceramic materials and components, with over fifty-five years of
operating history. We have concentrated on electronic ceramic materials and components
throughout our history. We have built a product portfolio across four categories — electronic and
ceramic materials, electronic components, telecommunication (“telecom”) components and
equipment components — forming a business framework that spans foundational materials,
critical components and high-end devices and assemblies across key application areas including
telecom, AI and data centers, consumer electronics, automotive electronics, semiconductor
manufacturing and packaging, new energy and intelligent industrial control.
We operate an integrated business model across materials and processes. Specifically, we
possess solid R&D capabilities in critical upstream raw materials formulations and implement
iterative optimization of technological processes of key manufacturing stages. At the same time,
we have large batch production capabilities with high-standard quality control, reinforcing core
advantages in supply and cost controllability.
Our R&D organization includes research institutes and business-unit technical teams,
covering raw material formulation as well as forming and sintering processes. We hold numerous
patents and participate in formulation and revision of various industry standards. We seek to
translate materials and process R&D into manufacturable product platforms. Regarding
production, we have multiple domestic production bases and strategic overseas sites enabling
cross-base capacity allocation, complemented by a sales network covering key global markets.
With respect to customers, we maintain long-term relationships with key customers across
our primary end markets, integrating localized services with global standards to strengthen
customer stickiness.
We have developed a diversified product portfolio that integrates mature product lines with
high-growth potential offerings. This matrix enables us to stabilize our revenue base while
capturing growth opportunities across core business scenarios. Regarding management, our
experienced and stable management team, together with a system covering systems,
mechanisms and culture, provides strong support for our continued focus on the electronic
ceramic materials business.

Electronic and Ceramic Materials
We focus on upstream foundational materials for the electronics value chain. Our portfolio
includes alumina (aluminum oxide) ceramic substrates, aluminum nitride ceramic substrates,
electronic pastes and solid oxide fuel cell (“SOFC”) electrolyte sheets.
As core upstream materials, these products are deployed across consumer electronics,
automotive electronics and new energy applications. Together, these products support electronic
component manufacturing and new-energy fuel cell applications. In particular:
• alumina ceramic substrates are used as base materials for chip resistors in consumer
electronics, providing electrical insulation, heat dissipation and mechanical support;
• electronic paste series — including resistive, mask, conductor and G2 encapsulated
pastes — are used for electrode printing in precision electronic components; and
• SOFC electrolyte sheets enable oxygen-ion transport while isolating fuel and oxidant,
facilitating direct electrochemical conversion of chemical energy to electricity under
high-temperature conditions and serving as a core component for SOFCs.
Electronic Components
Our electronic components portfolio comprises multilayer ceramic chip capacitors
(“MLCCs”), multilayer ceramic chip inductors (“MLCIs”) and fixed resistors. Capacitors, inductors
and resistors are foundational passive components broadly used across electronic circuits.
MLCCs are currently the primary revenue driver within this category. Leveraging our technical
capabilities accumulated over the years and our continued investment in R&D, we have
expanded our product lineup and scaled up supply to support diverse applications, while
supplying MLCCs, MLCIs and resistors in a coordinated manner to meet customers' one-stop
procurement service needs and enhance the compatibility of multi-category components.
Demand growth has been supported by technology iteration and application upgrades,
particularly inAI and data centers and automotive electronics, according to Frost & Sullivan. This
has increased requirements for high-end passive components.

We focus on technology, delivery, customer access and capacity:
• Technology. Our high-end MLCCs have achieved a dielectric layer thickness of
approximately one micrometer and stacking layers exceeding 1,000, laying the
foundation for our entry into advanced application scenarios includingAI data centers,

• Delivery. We rely on highly automated, end-to-end production to support the delivery

• Customers. We have obtained certifications from key customers across various core

• Capacity. We have expanded our production capacity as our orders increase and have
achieved large-scale mass production.
We believe that our success in these aspects enables us to benefit from industry growth and
market share gains.
Telecom Components
We focus on core needs in optical communication components and semiconductor-related
packaging, and have formed a diversified product matrix covering optical interconnects,
packaging parts as well as crystal oscillator packaging. Our portfolio includes ceramic ferrules
and sleeves, ceramic packages (“PKGs”), mechanical transfer (“MT”) ferrules and MT short
jumpers, and optical communication ceramic packages. These products correspond to different
key nodes in the communications value chain and together constitute our comprehensive supply
capabilities in telecom,AI and data centers, and semiconductor manufacturing and packaging.
Our telecom component product offering is a core lever for consolidating our position in
optical communications while expanding into semiconductor manufacturing and packaging.
• Ceramic ferrules and sleeves provide high-precision alignment to reduce signal loss
for high-speed broadband access, enabling precise fiber mating and serving
fiber-to-the-home (“FTTH”), 5G telecom base stations and data centers.
• In response to the high-density, high-bandwidth interconnect needs arising from the
rapid growth of AI and data centers. MT ferrules and MT short jumpers offer
low-latency, high-reliability optical communication solutions and act as key enablers of
the digital economy.
• Meanwhile, our PKGs address the high hermeticity and stability packaging
requirements of crystal oscillator whose downstream applications span automobiles,
smartphones, telecom base stations and laptops.
As end devices in segments such as automotive and IoT continue to become more
intelligent and connected, demand for crystal oscillator is increasing, which in turn supports
sustained growth in PKG demand, according to Frost & Sullivan.
Our telecom components have established notable competitiveness.
• According to Frost & Sullivan, our ceramic ferrules and sleeves accounted for
approximately 70% of the global market in terms of revenue in 2025;

BUSINESS
• According to Frost & Sullivan, our PKGs accounted for approximately 40% of the

• Our MT ferrules and MT short jumpers as well as optical communication ceramic
packages are gradually entering the supply chains of high-speed optical modules and
high-end optical devices.
Equipment Components
Our equipment components portfolio includes piezo microdispensing systems,
pan-semiconductor ceramic components, hermetic terminal for compressors, ceramic capillaries
and SOFC stacks. Drawing on accumulated core technologies in materials formulation and
forming capabilities, we provide products that address localization and energy-transition needs
while also serving steady industrial demand.
These products are used across several areas such as semiconductor manufacturing and
packaging, new energy and intelligent industrial control.
• Hermetic terminal for compressors deliver high hermetic sealing and dielectric strength
for compressors used in air conditioners, refrigerators and vehicles;
• Ceramic capillaries are bonding tools used in wire bonders for semiconductor
packaging;
• SOFC stacks extend from our SOFC accumulated expertise in this field and are
designed for distributed power generation;
• Pan-semiconductor ceramic components meet the high requirements for purity and
precision by advanced manufacturing; and
• Piezo microdispensing systems fulfill precision dispensing requirements in industrial
automation and robotics.
Other Products
Beyond our core product offerings, we leverage materials and process know-how to extend
product development into additional applications, primarily including ceramic appearance parts
and bioceramics. These extensions complement our core product portfolio and broaden our
market opportunities.

for high-end passive components. According to Frost & Sullivan, the global markets for core
electronic ceramic materials, core ceramic electronic components, core ceramic telecom
components and core ceramic equipment components are projected to grow from 2026 at a

Our Management and Corporate Culture
With over half a century of commitment in electronic ceramics, we have developed a
management and corporate culture aligned with our materials-centric business approach. Such
approach anchors strategic direction in core values while relying on institutionalized
management to support execution efficiency.

approach. We leverage digital systems to connect end-to-end operating processes and use
standardization to support efficiency. Our performance assessments and incentive mechanisms
are results-oriented and emphasize both steady achievement of business objectives and
collaborative capability building across teams. Dedicated mechanisms are in place to encourage
R&D innovation, reinforcing a virtuous cycle between technology advancement and talent
development.
Culturally, we not only emphasize respect for professionalism and commitment to quality,
promote the collaborative sharing and reuse of technology and resources with an open mindset,
but also attach importance to building a growth platform for employees, forging team synergy
while supporting individual development.
These practices align with our long-term objectives: to provide solutions that address
customer requirements, to build development pathways for employees, to create value for
shareholders, and to contribute to society. We aim to embed steady growth and pursuit of
excellence into daily operations to navigate industry cycles and market changes.

Aparticipant in electronic ceramic materials and components, with multiple core products
maintaining substantial global market shares
With over fifty-five years of deep focus on ceramic materials, we have multiple core
products that, protected by strong technological moats and scale advantages, maintain positions
in global markets. According to Frost & Sullivan, our ceramic ferrules and sleeves account for

global supplier and serving as a key enabler for the localization of crystal oscillator packaging. As
a major global manufacturer of SOFC electrolyte sheets, we supply international fuel cell
companies and are an indispensable core material supplier in the global fuel cell value chain.
We have achieved a critical leap from R&D breakthroughs to volume production, emerging
as a core force disrupting the dominant position of overseas manufacturers and ensuring the
autonomy and controllability of the domestic supply chain. In MLCCs — a high-end segment
previously reliant on imports in China — we have achieved advances in dielectric thinning,
reducing the dielectric layer thickness to approximately one micrometer, and scaled up stacking
layers to over 1,000, covering mainstream case sizes and offering full-series product support.
Our MLCCs have obtained qualification certifications from multiple benchmark customers, and
the application of our MLCCs has expanded from traditional home appliances and consumer
electronics to higher-end scenarios such as automotive electronics, telecom base stations andAI
servers. According to Frost & Sullivan, against a backdrop of sustained demand for high-end
capacitors and accelerated domestic substitution, the addressable market is substantial.

An integrated business layout and large-scale production capabilities jointly delivering
supply chain autonomy, efficiency and resilience
We operate an integrated system centered on materials and processes. Upstream, we
independently develop formulas of key raw materials such as ceramic powders and metal pastes.
In core processing, we master critical processes including tape casting and
reduction-atmosphere sintering. This collaborative system underpins large-scale production,
enabling end-to-end autonomy and control from materials to end applications. This integrated
layout reduces external dependence, mitigates cost volatility risks, enables rapid response to
downstream iterative demands, and supports supply-chain stability and operating efficiency.
Our end-to-end business model enhances autonomy and strengthens our supply chain’s
resilience to external risks. On raw materials, we advance in-house formula R&D for key raw
materials to secure stable supply at the source and achieve cost advantages. On capacity, by
leveraging production bases covering major domestic clusters and key overseas markets, and
supported by digital dynamic scheduling systems, we can flexibly respond to regional policy and
market fluctuations, significantly improving the stability of global order execution and the overall
risk resilience of the supply chain.
Our integration is designed to drive cost optimization and operational efficiency
improvements. By aligning our materials and processes, we reduce process tuning losses and
production downtime, improving overall throughput. Process improvement requirements feed
directly into equipment iterations, creating a self-reinforcing cycle from process optimization to
cost reduction.
Given the wide variety of our products and the extended process chain, we have
established a large-scale manufacturing system. Standardized workflows, optimized shop-floor
layouts, refined task segmentation, and specialized training and qualification for critical
processes allow efficient parallel production across product families. Modular production layouts,
digital management, and intelligent scheduling systems enable dynamic resource allocation
among product specifications and production sites. This supports continuous production output
for high-volume standard products while meeting batch delivery requirements for customized
products. We have historically fulfilled peak-season demand without record of large-scale
delayed deliveries.

BUSINESS
We also emphasize cross-stage technology and process reuse to enhance product
performance and facilitate collaborative innovation. Our platform covers the preparation of new
ceramic and composite materials; forming methods such as extrusion, dry pressing, tape casting,
and injection molding; equipment technologies including thin-film and coating technologies; and
sintering techniques such as oxidizing, reducing-atmosphere, and high-temperature co-firing. We
tailor raw material formulations and forming schemes to product-specific requirements, ensuring
that material properties and designed structures are accurately reflected in finished products.
Cross-stage reuse helps break down internal technical silos, enabling end-to-end optimization
and enhancing product performance.
Our quality control is embedded throughout the entire chain, from incoming material
inspection to in-process control and final product testing. For incoming materials, we implement
strict sampling and consistency checks on key inputs. During production, we assign dedicated
equipment, personnel, and parameters to critical processes. We monitor process parameters in
real time to enable automatic pass/fail judgment and exception alerts. These measures establish
a real-time closed loop for monitoring, judging, and addressing issues promptly as they arise. All
products are supported by physical error-proofing and in-process self-inspection mechanism,
helping maintain consistent performance and quality across batches in large-scale production.
We implement cost management through bulk procurement of key inputs, continuous
process optimization, automation upgrades, and scrap recycling, mitigating the cost complexity
associated with multi-product and multi-process operations. An end-to-end cost accounting and
control system supports ongoing production cost optimization during capacity expansion. From
2023 to 2025, our average gross margin remained stable at approximately 40% and our net profit
margin at approximately 30%, which are significantly higher than that of the industry average for
electronic ceramic materials and components, according to Frost & Sullivan.

In-depth global network layout jointly enabling balanced cost management and market

We deploy a global network that dynamically balances cost management with market

Technical accumulation building full-chain innovation moats, linking material
fundamentals to a closed loop of commercialization
Drawing on over fifty-five years of expertise in ceramic materials, we have established a
dual-core R&D structure comprising research institutes and business-unit technical teams,
including seven global R&D centers covering the entire innovation chain—from material

Electronic and Ceramic Materials
We offer a broad range of electronic materials, which are specialized substances
engineered for their distinct electrical, thermal, magnetic and optical properties, customizable for
various electronic components. Our major products include ceramic substrates (including
alumina ceramic substrates and aluminum nitride ceramic substrates), electronic pastes, ceramic
rods and metallized ceramics. We also offer SOFC electrolyte sheets, which are made of ceramic
materials.
Together, these products form a supply system of foundation materials that serve electronic
component manufacturing and new-energy fuel cell applications. As core upstream materials, our
electronic and ceramic materials are deployed across key use cases in electronic component
manufacturing and energy transition. By aligning product design with downstream application
requirements and addressing specific pain points, we have built a durable competitive position
while providing critical material support for the upgrading of the global electronics industry and
the implementation of new-energy strategies.
Ceramic Substrates
Our ceramic substrates are base materials made of ceramic
compounds, including alumina and aluminum nitride, used
to mount other materials to produce electronic components.
Our substrates feature high flexural strength, electrical
insulation, dielectric strength and temperature resistance,
as well as low coefficient of thermal expansion and
dielectric loss.
Our alumina ceramic substrates are primarily used as the base material for chip resistors,
with broad applications across various electronic circuits. They are also used for LED, high
voltage focusing potentiometer, small potentiometer, crystal oscillator, thick film integrated
circuit, as well as direct bonded/electroplated copper substrate for power electronics, all critical
components for applications such as electric vehicles (“EVs”) and industrial automation
equipment.
Our alumina ceramic substrates combine high insulation, high-temperature resistance and
tight dimensional tolerances, helping to resolve stability constraints of base materials amid
ongoing miniaturization and higher power density trends in electronic components. They address
urgent needs for high-performance foundational materials in end markets such as consumer
electronics and industrial control.
– 145 –

=== PAGE 155 ===
BUSINESS
Our aluminum nitride ceramic substrates are used as the base material for high power
electronics modules such as automotive-grade high-power LED, high-power insulated-gate
bipolar transistors for EVs, high-voltage power metal–oxide–semiconductor field-effect
transistors, radio frequency (“RF”) power loads, and lead resistors. Focusing on the thermal
bottlenecks of high-power devices, aluminum nitride ceramic substrates deliver efficient heat
management for applications including new energy vehicles and high-end industrial control
equipment, aligning with the migration of power electronics toward higher integration and power
density. Due to ceramic materials possessing high compressive strength, high mechanical
strength and good temperature resistance, ceramic substrates can withstand temperatures
ranging from 25 to 1000℃ and voltages ranging from 15 to 20 Kv/mm, making them suitable for
high-power and high-voltage applications.
Electronic Pastes
Our electronic paste products primarily include resistive
pastes, mask pastes, conductor pastes and G2
encapsulated pastes, which are mainly applied to ceramic
substrates for the manufacturing of chip resistors.
• Resistive paste is a key material used in the production of thick film resistors, such as
chip resistors and cylindrical resistors. Thick film resistors are essential components
for various electronic circuits and manufactured by screen-printing the resistive paste
uniformly onto ceramic substrates. Our resistive pastes feature excellent storage
stability and consistent performance.
• Mask paste is used in the screen-printing process of thick film resistors to provide
effective masking and protection. It demonstrates good water-washability and complies
with environmental standards.
• Conductor paste is applied to both the front and back electrodes of chip resistors. It
offers low sheet resistance and good storage stability.
• G2 encapsulated paste is specifically developed for chip resistors to provide protective
encapsulation of the resistive element. It also features low sheet resistance and stable
storage properties.
Engineered for excellent electrical conductivity and process compatibility, our electronic
pastes are designed to improve print uniformity and durability of electrodes in precision
components, supporting fine-pitch, high-yield and scalable manufacturing of electronic
components.

=== PAGE 156 ===
BUSINESS
SOFC Electrolyte Sheets
We provide ceramic electrolyte sheets for SOFC. The
SOFC electrolyte sheets are a ceramic functional
component fabricated from doped ceramic powders
combined with specific organic additives and processed into
defined shapes and dimensions. As a critical material of
SOFCs, the primary function of the electrolyte sheet is to
facilitate the transport of oxygen ions between the cathode
and anode, while effectively isolating the fuel from the
oxidant.
According to Frost & Sullivan, the continued advancement and commercialization of SOFC
technology are expected to drive increasing demand for high-performance electrolyte sheets.
Our electrolyte sheets target the core challenges of sustaining ionic conductivity and structural
stability at elevated temperatures, providing key material support for the commercialization of
SOFC technology amid the global energy transition and the increasing hydrogen utilization.
SOFCs operate at elevated temperatures, which present significant challenges to material
stability. Our electrolyte sheet products are engineered to address these challenges and offer a
long service life, along with the following key advantages: excellent chemical stability at high
temperatures, high mechanical strength, ionic conductivity, strong resistance to aging, as well as
high dimensional accuracy and surface flatness. These attributes contribute to the reliable and
efficient operation of SOFCs in demanding applications.
Other Major Electronic and Ceramic Materials
Ceramic Rods
Our ceramic rods are available in cylindrical and tubular
forms, and are primarily used in the manufacturing of
carbon film resistors, metal film resistors, metal oxide film
resistors, glass glaze resistors, wire-wound resistors, and
cement resistors. These ceramic rods serve as the base
material for the deposition of conductive films or the winding
of resistance wires.
Our ceramic rods are characterized by high mechanical strength, excellent electrical
insulation properties, and precise dimensional control, with strict quality standards applied to
surface appearance and defect minimization.
Metallized Ceramics
Our metallized ceramic products include alumina ceramics,
zirconia ceramics, and steatite ceramics, and can be
metallized with materials such as silver, silver-palladium,
molybdenum-manganese, and tungsten. The metallized
surface can be further electroplated with nickel, tin, or gold
to ensure excellent solderability. Products can be
custom-designed and manufactured based on specific
customer requirements.

Electronic Components
We began our electronic components business line with fixed resistors and have expanded
to MLCCs and MLCIs. Within this portfolio, MLCCs are currently the flagship of our electronic
components segment and the primary driver of revenue growth. Leveraging our self-developed
ceramic powder formula, we continue to upgrade performance while optimizing cost of our
MLCCs. This, combined with a broad product lineup, stable quality and scalable supply, enables
us to support customers across diversified applications at scale. In addition, our MLCCs, MLCIs
and fixed resistors are supplied in a coordinated manner to enable one-stop procurement,
alleviating fragmentation across multiple passive component categories, improving
cross-category fit, and enhancing customers’supply chain efficiency.
MLCCs
MLCCs are one of the most widely used passive electronic
components, found in virtually every electronic device produced
today, according to Frost & Sullivan. As a type of capacitor,
which is an electrical device that stores and releases electric
charge, MLCCs are critical for filtering noise, stabilizing voltage,
and storing energy in electric circuits.
Modern electronics demand smaller, lighter and more powerful components. MLCCs are
highly compact and offer high capacitance in a miniature footprint, making them ideal for
smartphones, laptops and other portable devices. This has driven explosive demand, with
high-end smartphones containing more than a thousand MLCCs and EVs using several
thousands, according to Frost & Sullivan.
We have made significant breakthroughs in both high capacitance and miniaturization,
enabling higher performance in a smaller footprint. Our high-end MLCCs have a dielectric layer
thickness as low as one micrometer, which allows us to pack a higher total capacitance into a
smaller case with stacking layers of over 1,000, achieving greater capacitance density. These
require incredibly precise manufacturing technology, including super-fine ceramic powder and
advanced printing and lamination techniques.
We offer a comprehensive MLCC portfolio comprising commercial grade MLCCs and
automotive MLCCs for diverse applications, and our products have been certified and adopted by
leaders in various industries, having undergone through stringent and extensive qualification
processes. Our MLCC roadmap is use-case centric and targets specific pain points in
downstream applications. Part-number coverage spans multiple performance dimensions to
address diverse operating conditions and design constraints across end markets. Customers of
our MLCC include leading manufacturers across major downstream sectors such as home
appliances, networking and telecom base stations, security, and automotive-grade applications.
Our MLCCs are widely used in automotive electronics, consumer electronics, intelligent
industrial control, telecom, and AI and data centers. The line-up includes miniaturized,
high-voltage, high-capacitance, high-strength, and high-frequency MLCC series, with varying
sizes and voltage specifications for each series to satisfy diverse customers’needs.
• Miniaturized MLCCs. High reliability, suitable for various electronic devices operating
in confined spaces such as smartphones.

=== PAGE 158 ===
BUSINESS
• High-Voltage MLCCs. Utilizing optimized ceramic structure design, these capacitors
can withstand medium to high voltage environments (approximately 100V to 2000V).
They are widely used in industrial power systems, lighting equipment, home
appliances, and other fields, meeting the higher power and voltage requirements of
advanced equipment.
• High-Capacitance MLCCs. Designed specifically for space-constrained, highly
integrated systems such as smart electronic products andAI servers, these capacitors
provide higher capacitance values within compact package sizes, balancing limited
internal volume with higher performance requirements.
• High-Strength MLCCs.
o High-Strength F Series. These capacitors feature a special flexible resin layer
on the electrodes, which can withstand mechanical stresses such as board
flexing, drop impacts, and thermal shocks, preventing cracking and short-circuit
faults. They are widely used in automotive electronics and industrial power
systems.
o High-Strength S Series. By adding a high-strength ceramic layer to the surface,
these capacitors significantly increase mechanical strength, greatly reducing the
risk of product fracture during normal use. They are designed to withstand harsh
operating conditions and are widely used in home appliances and lighting
industries.
o High-Strength Z Series. These capacitors have metal supports added to both
ends of traditional MLCCs, which reduce the risk of cracks forming in the
capacitor when subjected to mechanical stress on the circuit board. They also
lower the risk of cracks during soldering and reduce noise caused by the
piezoelectric effect. They are widely used in industrial power systems and lighting
equipment.
• High-Frequency MLCCs. As Class I capacitors, these products exhibit highly stable
electrical performance under varying temperatures, voltages, and over time. The
internal electrodes have low resistivity, achieving low equivalent series resistance and
high quality characteristics at high frequencies. They are suitable for low-loss,
high-stability circuits, such as filters, resonators, and timing circuits.
MLCIs
Our MLCIs are compact inductive components manufactured
with a multi-layer ceramic process similar to MLCCs. Designed to
resist rapid changes in current, they are used predominantly in
high-frequency circuits — for example, RF front-end filtering,
impedance matching, and frequency tuning in connectivity,
handset, and IoT applications. Strategically, MLCIs are a focus
area for future development given their tighter integration with
high-frequency, miniaturized system architectures and the
structural demand from 5G/AIoT devices. Leveraging our ceramic materials, multilayer printing,
and sintering know-how accumulated from MLCC manufacturing, we target improved Q factor,
low DC resistance, and stable inductance over temperature and bias. Commercially, our initial

Resistors
Our resistor products are primarily fixed resistors used for
current limiting and voltage division across a broad range of
electronic circuits, including energy-saving lamps, LED lighting,
electronic rectifiers, chargers, household appliances, and
instruments and meters. They feature high resistance accuracy,
excellent voltage withstand capability, tight temperature
coefficients, and stable reliability under high-voltage pulse and
humidity load conditions.
Telecom Components
We offer a range of telecom components, including ceramic ferrules and sleeves, MT
ferrules and MT short jumpers, optical communication ceramic packages and aluminum nitride
(“AlN”) submounts, to enable both current and next-generation of telecom and AI infrastructure.
We also provide PKGs, which are critical for telecom electronics. Our telecom components
portfolio underpins our position in optical communications while expanding into semiconductor
packaging.
Ceramic Ferrules and Sleeves
Ceramic ferrules are essential components used in the
connection of optical communication components. Their primary
function is to enable the precise physical alignment of optical
fibers, typically in detachable fiber optic connections. Ceramic
sleeves are commonly used in conjunction with ferrules to
ensure accurate positioning and stable coupling.
Fiber optic connectors represent the most important application of our ceramic ferrules. A
typical connector consists of two mated ferrules, each holding the end of an optical fiber, inserted
into a common sleeve. This configuration allows for high-precision fiber-to-fiber alignment,
ensuring efficient signal transmission. These components are widely used at connection points,
splitters, and termination points throughout optical networks.
Ceramic ferrules and sleeves are widely used in optical modules and optical transceivers,
where compact form factors, high-speed data transmission, and long-term reliability are
essential. Within these devices, ceramic ferrules and sleeves function as high-precision
alignment structures, ensuring stable optical coupling between internal components — such as
laser diodes, photodetectors, and optical fibers. Thanks to their exceptional dimensional
accuracy, thermal stability, and mechanical durability, ceramic ferrules and sleeves help maintain
consistent optical performance across a wide range of operating conditions. This is particularly
critical for minimizing signal loss and insertion loss, ensuring stable data transmission, and
supporting long-term device performance in high-density, high-bandwidth environments such as
data centers, 5G networks, and cloud computing infrastructure.
– 150 –

=== PAGE 160 ===
BUSINESS
Given the need for precise signal transmission, ceramic ferrules must meet extremely high
standards of concentricity and dimensional accuracy. As a critical component, the performance of
the ceramic ferrule directly affects the overall reliability and efficiency of optical devices.
Our ceramic ferrules are manufactured to sub-micron precision, with tolerances of less than
1μm. They offer a range of performance advantages, including high concentricity and
dimensional accuracy, low insertion loss, excellent mechanical strength, wear and aging
resistance and long operational lifespan.
Our products are deeply aligned with three core deployment scenarios — FTTH, 5G telecom
base stations and data centers — providing precision alignment, signal integrity and
high-reliability interconnects for both current and next-generation telecom andAI infrastructure.
In FTTH deployments, ceramic ferrules and sleeves provide high-precision alignment that
minimizes insertion loss at subscriber access points for residential and commercial broadband,
supporting the ongoing upgrade in access bandwidth.
In 5G telecom base station environments, our optical connection components deliver
consistent environmental adaptability and signal stability to support high-density site rollouts and
long-reach optical links amid continuous 5G build-out and technology iterations.
In data centers, MT ferrules with short jumpers and ceramic ferrules enable low-latency,
high-reliability optical connectivity for high-density, high-bandwidth architectures driven by
accelerating compute demand.
PKGs
Manufactured in small, low-profile form factors, our PKGs are
primarily designed as the “case” that protects resonators and
oscillators, while enabling surface-mount integration onto a
printed circuit board (“PCB”).
By leveraging PKGs, we are extending into the crystal device
packaging domain, addressing stringent needs for hermeticity
and stability in resonator and oscillator packaging. This helps
mitigate reliance on imported core packaging materials in the domestic crystal industry, aligns
with device miniaturization and rising precision timing requirements, and opens growth
opportunities in semiconductor packaging.
These packages provide a stable platform for mounting resonators and oscillators, offering
reliable protection against mechanical damage and environmental factors such as moisture and
corrosive gases, thereby ensuring hermetic sealing. In addition, the metal bonding pads on the
ceramic base enable reliable electrical connections between internal components and external
circuitry, supporting miniaturization, ultra-thin profiles and high assembly efficiency.
Resonators and oscillators are frequency control components, which are used in all
electronic devices that require precise timing or frequency control. We also offer PKGs for
surface acoustic wave (“SAW”) filters, commonly used in RF applications. These components are
primarily used in smartphones, wireless communication, GPS, Bluetooth, automotive electronics
and other related applications. For example, a single smartphone contains several different types
of resonators, oscillators and filters to manage its various functions.

BUSINESS
MT Ferrules and MT Short Jumpers
We offer a full range of MT ferrules in various specifications and
models, along with corresponding guide pins, which are
customizable to meet customer-specific requirements. These
components are primarily used in multi-fiber push-on/pull-off
(“MPO”) and multi-fiber termination push-on (“MTP”) connectors,
as well as in high-speed optical module assemblies.
MPO and MTP connectors are high-density fiber optic connector systems widely used in
modern optical communication networks. They are designed to enable the simultaneous
connection of multiple optical fibers, such as 12 fibers, within a single compact interface,
significantly increasing data transmission capacity while reducing space and installation
complexity.
The mating accuracy of these connectors is determined by the positional accuracy of the
MT ferrules and the outer diameter precision of the guide pins. These factors are critical in
ensuring low insertion loss and consistent optical performance in high-density, high-bandwidth
applications, such as data centers, telecom networks and high-speed computing environments.
In addition, we offer MT short jumpers primarily used for multi-channel optical interconnects
between the external optical interface of optical transceiver modules and the internal optical
chips. By providing multiple parallel transmission channels at a fixed per-channel data rate, they
increase the overall transmission rate of the transceiver module.
Optical Communication Ceramic Packages
Optical communication ceramic packages are key components
used in optical device modules that house critical optoelectronic
components, such as laser diodes and photodetectors.
Engineered for precise opto-mechanical alignment and long-term
reliability under extreme temperature, humidity, corrosion and
vibration, these packages support the migration toward
higher-rate, higher-density optical modules in telecom and AI
and data center networks.
Our products provide mechanical support and optical alignment, and are engineered to
withstand high temperatures, high humidity, corrosion and vibration, ensuring stable performance
under extreme conditions and over long operating lifespans. They are widely adopted in
long-haul optical transceivers, tunable laser modules and optical amplifiers, including
applications in next-generation optical transceivers.
– 152 –

=== PAGE 162 ===
BUSINESS
Other Major Telecom Components
Field Mountable Fiber Optic Connectors
Field mountable fiber optic connectors can be directly assembled
onto optical fibers at the installation site. They are widely used in
fiber optic transmission lines, optical distribution frames and fiber
optic testing equipment, and have become one of the most
commonly adopted solutions in FTTH deployments.
Our products offer high mating precision, strong adaptability to fibers of varying outer
diameters, and utilize ceramic materials with low thermal expansion coefficients. These features
ensure stable mating interfaces without deformation, long service life, and simple assembly,
making them well-suited for efficient and reliable on-site fiber termination.
AlN Submounts
Our AlN submounts offer high thermal conductivity and excellent
electrical insulation, making them ideal for advanced optical
module applications. As high-power optical modules become
increasingly critical in AI infrastructure, efficient thermal
management is essential. Our AlN submounts effectively
dissipate heat, ensuring stable operation and extended lifespan
of core optoelectronic components. They are particularly
well-suited for use in compact, high-performance modules where
both thermal and space efficiency are crucial.
Equipment Components
Our equipment component portfolio includes piezo microdispensing systems,
pan-semiconductor ceramic components, hermetic terminal for compressors and ceramic
capillaries.
Our equipment components portfolio is positioned to capture growth in high-potential
sectors while enhancing business resilience through diversification. On one hand, we target
semiconductor and new energy domains with products that address supply gaps and support
industrial upgrading. On the other hand, we continue to provide stable, reliable support to
traditional industrial applications with stringent requirements for durability and safety.
Piezo Microdispensing Systems
Through Vermes Microdispensing GmbH (“Vermes”), which we
acquired in 2017, we offer contact-free piezo microdispensing
systems for many manufacturing processes. Advances in
miniaturization are making contactless micro-dispensing systems
indispensable for modern manufacturing processes, as they
require precise, repeatable and reliable dispensing of very small
amounts of liquids or pastes, such as adhesives and sealants,
onto a surface.
– 153 –

=== PAGE 163 ===
BUSINESS
We offer powerful piezo microdispensing systems, which have the ability to dispense large
numbers of very small and precise dots (up to sub-nanoliters) in a very short time. We supply the
consumer electronics, semiconductor, automotive, telecom, medical and pharmaceutical
industries with industry-specific dispensing solutions for adhesives, silicones, solder pastes, cell
suspensions and more. For example, our systems are used in the consumer electronics industry
to grease safety switches with very high viscous grease or to dispense conductive paste onto
thermocouples; and in the semiconductor industry, our systems are used for underfill
applications, which enables an optimal package design due to the minimal distance between the
chips.
Our contact-free micro-dispensing solutions address precision processing needs in
consumer electronics and semiconductor manufacturing by improving placement accuracy and
throughput. A broad, application-specific valve portfolio also helps optimize customer takt time
and enriches our product mix, mitigating exposure to single-segment volatility.
Pan-Semiconductor Ceramic Components
Our pan-semiconductor ceramic components are widely used in
processing equipment across the semiconductor, display panel,
LED, and PV industries. Engineered with high-purity ceramics
and tight dimensional control, these components help minimize
contamination, deliver stable mechanical and thermal
performance, and support long-term tool uptime with reduced
unplanned maintenance.
Beyond core pan-semiconductor equipment, we also supply ceramic structural parts to new
energy and automotive equipment makers. These products are designed for stringent corrosion,
wear, and thermal-shock requirements, and can be customized to meet application-specific
CTQs.
By combining high material purity with precision machining and surface finishing, our
pan-semiconductor ceramic components meet demanding specs from semiconductor and display
equipment OEMs, helping lower particle and metal ion risks while enabling domestic equipment
performance upgrades and localization progress across the broader pan-semiconductor
ecosystem.
SOFC Stacks
We also offer SOFC stacks that advance the commercialization
of solid oxide fuel cells amid the global energy transition.
The SOFC stack is the core component of an SOFC system,
functioning as the device that directly converts chemical energy
from fuels such as hydrogen or natural gas into electrical energy
through electrochemical reactions. Operating at high
temperatures, SOFCs offer high energy conversion efficiency,
fuel flexibility and low emissions, making them well-suited for a
range of applications including distributed power generation and clean energy solutions for
industrial and residential use.
– 154 –

=== PAGE 164 ===
BUSINESS
An SOFC stack uses several dozen power generation cells which are joined together in
series. Each cell is a uniquely designed cylindrical flat plate structure, and the resulting stack
achieves excellent durability, low internal resistance and high-power generation efficiency,
leveraging our ceramic materials and proprietary manufacturing technologies.
With growing global demand for low-carbon and sustainable energy solutions, SOFC
technology is gaining traction as a key enabler in the transition to cleaner energy systems. Our
products are designed to support this shift by delivering reliable and scalable fuel cell solutions to
meet diverse market needs.
Other Major Equipment Components
Hermetic Terminal for Compressors
Hermetic terminal for compressors are one of the core
components of compressors, serving as critical electrical
elements that ensure both insulation and hermetic sealing.
These components must withstand high internal pressure while
maintaining excellent gas tightness and high dielectric strength,
and therefore are subject to stringent safety requirements.
The key technologies in the production of hermetic terminal for compressors lie in the
formulation of glass frit and the sealing process. Reliable sealing is essential to maintaining the
overall stability and performance of the product, enabling compressors to operate safely even
under harsh environmental conditions.
We possess comprehensive technical capabilities across the entire production chain,
including product design, glass powder formulation, controlled-atmosphere sintering, and
electrical welding. Our hermetic terminal for compressors feature excellent high-pressure
hermeticity, dielectric and mechanical strength, outstanding thermal shock resistance,
environmental durability, and high reliability.
As a result, our products are widely used in compressors for residential and commercial
applications, such as air conditioners and refrigerators, as well as in compressors designed for
special industrial environments and new energy vehicles.
These attributes make our hermetic terminal for compressors well-suited for compressors
used in home appliances and automotive air-conditioning systems operating under complex duty
cycles, addressing the industry’s non-negotiable reliability requirements.
Ceramic Capillaries
Ceramic capillaries are high-precision ceramic components used
as bonding tools (welding tips) in wire bonders, playing a critical
role in the wire bonding process for semiconductor packaging.
These components enable the formation of reliable electrical
interconnections between integrated circuits (“ICs”) and package
leads.
– 155 –

=== PAGE 165 ===
BUSINESS
According to Frost & Sullivan, we are the first company in China to achieve large-scale,
mass production of ceramic capillaries. Our products are widely used in the wire bonding of LED
chips, diodes, transistors and ICs.
Leveraging our proprietary high-durability ceramic materials and advanced manufacturing
technologies, characterized by exceptional precision and dimensional uniformity, our ceramic
capillaries help enhance bonding accuracy, improve production yield, and increase overall
efficiency in semiconductor assembly processes.
As one of the earliest large-scale domestic producers, we help address critical tooling
availability for wire bonding, supporting higher bonding accuracy, yield improvement and
efficiency gains in semiconductor assembly.
Other Products
To serve our customers’ various needs and to maintain a diversified product portfolio, we
also offer other products, including ceramic appearance parts, bioceramics, other ceramic
structural parts and other related products.
CeramicAppearance Parts
Our ceramic appearance parts are high-performance,
fine-ceramic parts designed for visible, user-facing applications
that require a combination of premium esthetics, precise
dimensional control, and reliable functional properties.
Leveraging our core strengths in ceramic powder engineering,
dry-pressing forming, injection molding, high-precision
machining and polishing, as well as advanced coating and
surface finishing, these components deliver hardness, scratch
resistance, and long-term color stability compared to
conventional metallic or polymer alternatives.
Our ceramic appearance parts are widely adopted in consumer electronics, smart home
devices, and high-end appliances.
Bioceramics
Our bioceramics portfolio is centered on orthopedic applications,
with a primary focus on hip joint solutions. Key applications
include ceramic components for hip arthroplasty — such as
femoral heads and acetabular liners — engineered for ultra-low
wear rates, smooth tribological interfaces, and durability under
cyclic loads. Leveraging zirconia-toughened alumina and tightly
controlled microstructures, we deliver biocompatibility,
mechanical reliability (strength, wear resistance, fracture
toughness), and long-term stability in physiological
environments. Guided by our R&D framework, we integrate formulation design, powder
processing, green-body shaping, precision sintering, and finishing into a vertically managed
platform aligned with stringent medical quality and regulatory requirements.

RESEARCH & DEVELOPMENT
R&D Strategy
We compete in a market characterized by rapid technology iteration, increasingly stringent
reliability standards and persistent cost reduction pressure, which subjects our R&D to
heightened challenges and requirements. Leveraging years of accumulated technological
know-how and large-scale mass production experience, we have established a tiered R&D
system featuring four layers — “one generation in mass production, one in reserve, one in
development and one in research,” — to systematically respond to rapid shifts in market and
industry demand.
For our current product portfolio, we focus on three core directions: (i) expanding
specification coverages and exploring new application scenarios to extend the product value
boundaries, (ii) iterating process technologies to enhance product performance and quality
control and (iii) advancing automation upgrades of production equipment and end-to-end
digitalized management, thereby strengthening our advantages in mass production efficiency,
cost and product quality.
We anchor our efforts in materials and remain guided by market and customer demand to
carry out future product portfolio planning. Through in-depth research into new products and
projects with strong technological potential and market prospects, we proactively reserve
next-generation core technologies and product solutions.
In parallel, we have established a multi-dimensional and full-cycle market feedback
mechanism spanning the entire lifecycle from product research, technology development to mass
production implementation and continuous product optimization and iteration, ensuring our R&D
directions remain aligned with broader industry development trends.
R&D Infrastructure
As of December 31, 2025, we maintain seven research institutes in multiple regions in
China and in Germany. Our R&D organization consists of research institute and business-unit
technical teams, covering the full spectrum from R&D, accumulation and integration of core
manufacturing process technologies across multiple product categories, optimization of product
performance and cost, to R&D and commercialization of new products and specifications.
These institutes concentrate on:
• Electronic and ceramic materials: high-strength, high-thermal-conductivity ceramic
substrates and PKGs; high-precision chip resistive pastes, high-precision printed
conductor pastes, high-temperature and co-fired conductor pastes and mask pastes.
• Electronic components: high-permittivity material systems for MLCC; high-frequency,
low-loss inductors; and high-capacitance, high-reliability MLCC technologies.
• Pan-semiconductor ceramic components: ceramic capillaries, anti-static handling
arms and electrostatic chucks.
• New energy ceramics: SOFC electrolyte sheets and stacks.
• Optical communications: single-mode/multi-mode low-loss MT ferrules; high-speed
optical communication ceramic packages and fiber optic connectors.
