BUSINESS
• Bioceramics: zirconia-toughened alumina ceramics.
• Processes: synthesis of highly dispersed nano-scale ceramic; ceramic forming and
multilayer ceramic processing; precision machining of ceramics; ceramic-metal
co-sintering; metallized ceramics; onlineAOI and reliability testing and analysis.
Representative Breakthroughs
• In MLCC, we continue to push high-capacitance and miniaturization by reducing
dielectric-layer thickness to one micrometer with enhanced powder performance and
controlled grain growth, and by scaling layer counts beyond 1,000 through improved
rheological properties of ceramic and metal pastes and high-continuity internal
electrodes. Our portfolio covers automotive, industrial control, telecom and consumer
electronics fields, including mid-to-high voltage parts (approximately 100–2000 V), soft
terminal and high-reliability structural enhancements to resist flexure cracking, as well as
high-frequency products with Cu internal electrodes. During the Track Record Period, we
introduced the M3Lseries and the “S” series, alongside soft terminal and high-frequency
innovations, and continued to extend the application scenarios of miniaturized and
high-voltage options across platforms.
• In optical communication, our zirconia ferrules and sleeves with sub-micron
concentricity, low insertion/return loss stability and excellent wear resistance are
engineered to meet the demand for 5G and high-reliability optical networks. In
response to demand for data center and high-speed AI interconnect needs, we have
expanded MT ferrules with tighter positional accuracy and diameter tolerance,
higher-density MPO/MTP connectors and high-frequency, high-speed PKGs.
• In ceramic packages, we provide high flatness, reliable metallization adhesion and
hermetic sealing solutions for Xtal/TSX/TF/OSC/TCXO and SAW devices. In the
meantime, we advanced AlN submounts by increasing thermal conductivity and
optimizing surface treatment processes to meet the thermal management demands of
compact high-power optical modules.
• In materials, we are scaling alumina ceramic substrates with high flexural strength,
dielectric strength and dimensional control for resistors, LEDs and power substrates,
and aluminum nitride ceramic substrates with high thermal conductivity and electrical
insulation for automotive power modules, HV MOSFETs, IGBTs and RF loads. Our
electronic pastes ecosystem includes resistive, mask, conductor and G2 encapsulated
pastes; by tuning rheology and adhesion, we enable high-yield printing for chip
resistors, while metallized ceramics using Mo-Mn, W, Ag and Ag-Pd with Ni/Sn/Au
electroplating stacks enable solderability and environmental durability.
• In SOFC, we develop electrolyte sheets and stack architectures that couple high ionic
conductivity with chemical stability at elevated temperatures and thermal-mechanical
durability for long life. Our stack design balances power density, durability and
reliability, while work on seals, interconnect materials and thermal cycling strategies
aims to minimize degradation and extend product lifetimes. We have collaborated with
a leading gas company in Shenzhen to undertake the first national 300kW SOFC
commercialization project, which proves stack durability and consistency in practical
implementation.

• In bioceramics, we progressed zirconia-toughened alumina materials for orthopedic
applications. Ceramic femoral heads and inserts were introduced at international

tribological performance, together with validation of manufacturing traceability and

• We also expanded pan-semiconductor ceramic components for semiconductor,

Intellectual Property and Know-how
We protect material formulations, process technology, multilayer architectures, metallization
schemes and application-specific structures through a combination of patents, trade secrets and
data governance. In addition, we serve leading players in various downstream industries who
have stringent requirements on quality, reliability, traceability and total cost of ownership, which
propels us to continuously improve our technological capabilities in line with downstream
demands. This includes powder synthesis parameters, sintering profiles, defect root-cause maps,
stack and termination tolerances, and reliability models — capabilities that underpin replicable
scale-up, faster qualification cycles across MLCCs, PKGs, optical ferrules, ceramic substrates
and SOFC stacks.
As of December 31, 2025, we had obtained 722 registered patents globally (including 200
utility model patents in the PRC, and 362 invention patents and 160 design patents globally), 10
software copyrights, 104 trademarks and four domain names in the PRC. As of the same date,
we also had 180 pending patent applications globally. As of the Latest Practicable Date, we had
registered 12 trademarks, one domain name and 17 patents which are material to our business.
R&D Expenditure and Team
We continue to invest in R&D to support a multi-product roadmap and strategic pivots into
high-reliability and new energy applications. Our R&D expenses were RMB545.8 million,
RMB583.1 million and RMB653.4 million in 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively.
As of December 31, 2025, we had 1,975 R&D personnel, representing 11.4% of our total
headcount. Our team comprises experienced engineers across mechanical, electrical, software,
process, and systems disciplines. Our R&D team has a high proportion of postgraduate talent,
with around 42.6% holding master’s degrees and approximately 1.5% holding doctoral degrees,
and a significant share being graduates of leading universities, as of December 31, 2025. The
overall structure has shifted toward a higher proportion of seasoned engineers, supporting faster
iteration from concept to pilot and further to mass production. Our R&D organization spans
materials science, ceramic processes, equipment engineering, analysis and metrology, and
reliability.

QUALITY CONTROL
We have comprehensive policies and detailed procedures in place to ensure product quality.
We have obtained a series of certificates including ISO 9001 for our quality management system,
IATF 16949 for our international standard for automotive quality management system, ISO 14001
for our environmental management system, IECQ Certificate for hazardous substance process
management system and other various domestic and global certificates for our specific products.
To ensure product quality, we have established quality control departments in each business
segment responsible for implementing quality control measures throughout the entire production
cycle, including raw material inspection, in-process quality control, and final product inspection.
We have built various quality control procedures and processes during our production process to
ensure that our product quality meets the expectations and requirements of each critical process,
and we monitor the product yield for each of our critical production processes.

Distribution
We sell a portion of MLCC, piezo microdispensing system and alumina ceramic substrates
through distributors, which allows us to efficiently manage the large number of end customers
across various industries and enhances our market penetration in mid-to-small sized customers.
The distributors are not exclusively engaged to distribute our products. Revenue from
distributorship increased from RMB1,147.7 million in 2023 to RMB1,560.2 million in 2024 and
further to RMB2,266.4 million in 2025. The increase was mainly attributable to our MLCC
business. We achieved technical breakthroughs and expanded capacity, progressively obtained
certifications from leading downstream customers, and experienced higher market acceptance,
which together led to an increase in the number of MLCC distributors and higher sales per
distributor. Given MLCC’s broad end-market applications and the industry practice that small and
mid-sized customers are typically served via distributors, we leveraged distributors’ networks to
reach a more diversified customer base while conserving direct sales resources.

• Pricing. Prices are generally specified in each purchase order issued in accordance
with our standard terms and conditions.
• Sub-distribution. Distributors are not allowed to sub-distribute in our name without
our prior written consent. During the Track Record Period, no instances of distributors
violating the foregoing provisions were identified.
• Warranty. Our warranty period varies from customers and product types, generally
ranging from one to five years, except for consumables.
• Product returns. We maintain a stringent product return policy which serves as a key
measure to mitigate the risk of channel stuffing and ensure the integrity of our
recognized sales revenue. We generally do not accept product returns from our
customers other than for documented product quality issues which are subject to our
quality assurance procedures. This policy is communicated to and contractually agreed
with all customers and distributors prior to any sale. Any exception to this policy for
non-quality reasons is rare and requires specific pre-approval from our senior
management, and is assessed on a stringent, case-by-case basis.
• Termination. The agreements will be terminated upon expiration. If either party
breaches the agreement, the non-breaching party shall have the right to terminate this
agreement.
To the best of our knowledge, all of our distributors are Independent Third Parties. The
distributors are not connected to any of our Company, our subsidiaries, our shareholders,
directors, senior management or any of their respective associates. To our best knowledge,
besides the ordinary course distribution arrangement with us, there is no other relationship
between the distributors and each of our Company, our subsidiaries, our shareholders, directors
or senior management or any of their respective associates. In general, our relationships with
distributors have remained stable. During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest
Practicable Date, we have no material unresolved disputes or lawsuits with our distributors.
We require distributors to file a report of the end-customers’ information to us prior to
initiating any customer development activities. During the Track Record Period, to our best
knowledge, no sub-distributors were engaged by our distributors. During the Track Record
Period, to our best knowledge, no distributors covered the same end-customer. As a result,
overlap among distributors is limited, which mitigates the risk of cannibalisation. We further
control channel stuffing risks through our internal management policies for distributors and
measures including regularly keeping track of distributors’ inventory information and
decomposing annual sales targets of our distributors into monthly plans to standardize order
placement. Specifically, if a distributor’s monthly procurement deviates significantly from the
plan, we perform verifications to mitigate channel stuffing risks and reserve the right to reject or
adjust orders. Furthermore, if a distributor exceeds its authorized credit limit, it must provide
– 165 –

=== PAGE 175 ===
BUSINESS
supplementary collateral or make prepayments. As such channel stuffing behavior objectively
increases a distributor’s liquidity pressure, it serves as a financial deterrent, and we have not
experienced any instances of channel stuffing by our distributors during the Track Record Period.
In September 2025, we engaged an internal control consultant to review our internal control
management system relating to the prevention of channel stuffing and to provide
recommendations for enhancement. Based on the review, the consultant identified certain
deficiencies and recommended that we strengthen our internal control measures. In response to
such recommendations, we further refined and strengthened our existing internal control
measures in relation to the prevention of channel stuffing under our existing control framework.
These enhanced measures included: (i) clarifying and formalizing our internal control
requirements and operational procedures relating to product return arrangements applicable to
distributors, including codifying the principle that returns or exchanges by distributors are
generally not permitted except in cases involving product quality issues; and (ii) further
enhancing our monitoring of distributor inventory levels by formalizing and supplementing in our
internal policies the procedures for collecting, reviewing and assessing inventory-related
information, and conducting analyses of inventory movements and turnover to identify unusual
fluctuations. Since adopting these measures, the consultant has not identified any significant
deficiencies in the follow-up review regarding internal control management system relating to the
prevention of channel stuffing. According to the review results, our Directors are of the view, and
the internal control consultant concurs, that our internal control management system relating to
channel stuffing controls, if implemented continuously, is adequate and effective in preventing
material risks in this area.
We manage potential cannibalisation through: (i) allocation of key accounts to a single
primary distributor or to our direct sales; (ii) periodic channel reviews assessing sell-through,
inventory and customer coverage; and (iii) contract provisions prohibiting channel stuffing,
including the right to refuse or adjust orders where inventory indicators exceed thresholds.
We do not set suggested retail prices for distributors. Distributors determine resale prices
independently based on market conditions, subject to applicable laws.
We generally set minimum purchase requirements for our distributors based on market
demand. This ensures those distributors have enough inventory for in-time delivery and confirms
their willingness to build a stable relationship with us and the end users. We terminated our
partnership with three and three distributors in 2023 and 2024 due to their failure to meet our
minimum purchase requirements.
Marketing
We position our brand around electronic ceramic materials and components and related
products to support the development of various industries, including telecom, AI and data
centers, consumer electronics, automotive electronics, semiconductor manufacturing and
packaging, new energy and intelligent industrial control. We maintain close and regular
interactions with customers to understand technical requirements and competitive benchmarks,
enabling us to position our products appropriately, resolve production issues promptly and deliver
satisfactory after-sales services. We collect feedback directly from customers and collaboration
partners to inform product iterations and operational improvements. We organize online and
offline marketing activities and participate in major domestic and international industry
conferences and exhibitions to enhance brand awareness and support business development.

SUPPLY CHAIN
Raw Materials and Procurement
We procure critical raw materials and auxiliaries from qualified global suppliers. During the
Track Record Period, our main raw materials are sourced domestically. Our raw material prices
fluctuate due to a variety of factors, including supply and demand dynamics, our ability to
negotiate prices with suppliers and others. We usually work with multiple suppliers to reduce
risks associated with product supply. During the Track Record Period, we did not experience any
significant shortage of raw material supplies, and the raw materials provided by our suppliers did
not have any significant quality issues.
Our Suppliers
We have established a comprehensive system for the selection and qualification of
suppliers to ensure the stability and reliability of our supply chain. We consider a number of
factors during our supplier selection and qualification process, including their financial condition,
business performance, industry reputation, ESG commitment and certifications. We also conduct
on-site visits to potential suppliers’ business premises before we decide to cooperate with the
suppliers. We monitor, in real time, the quality, delivery timeliness, and cost of each batch of
products from our suppliers, and we periodically conduct comprehensive evaluations of their
overall qualifications, including assessments of their raw material procurement, inventory status,
and any legal risks. We believe that our operation is not dependent on any particular supplier.
During the Track Record Period, we maintained qualified supplier pool to avoid overreliance on
any of our suppliers and we believe there is no significant difficulty in finding suitable substitutes
for our suppliers.

BUSINESS
The key terms of the long-term framework agreements we enter into with our suppliers
generally include the following:
• Duration. The duration of the supply agreement with our suppliers is typically one
year. Upon expiration, without mutual written agreement by both parties to terminate,
the term shall automatically be extended for an additional one year, and the same shall
apply thereafter on a rolling basis.
• Product specification. We specify the product name, specification, price, quantity,
delivery timeline and other detailed items in each purchase order we send to our
suppliers.
• Payment and credit term. Payment and credit terms are typically separately included
in each order that we place with the supplier.
• Logistics. Our suppliers are responsible for delivering qualifying products to our
designated locations.
• Quality guarantee. Products are typically accepted in accordance with our
specifications, as well as national, local and industry standards. Should any quality
issues arise during the warranty period, the supplier shall be responsible for
replacement or repair.
• Termination. The agreement will be terminated upon mutual written agreement. We
are entitled to terminate the agreement if we suffer significant losses due to the
supplier’s quality issues or complaints from our customers.

During the Track Record Period, we engaged in transactions with entities that are either on

purchased equipment, parts, accessories, and related services for those products from the
suppliers that are Relevant Entities. The sales and purchase with the Relevant Entities were
primarily settled in RMB, with only one Russian entity settled in US dollars. The banks involved
are all PRC domestic banks and are not subject to sanctions.

Sanctions and Export Control Compliance Measures
We have established and will continue to implement internal controls and risk management
measures related to sanctions and export control compliance, including but not limited to: (i)
establishing sanctions and export control related policies and standardizing procedures covering
business risk assessment and review, training and awareness, consultation and reporting,
investigations and supervision, and records management; (ii) conducting pre-engagement and
ongoing risk assessments, including Know-Your-Client due diligence on prospective customers
and suppliers (such as identity, business nature, ownership structure, geographic location, and
related parties), as well as initial and periodic screening against applicable restricted party and
country lists, and review and monitoring of product classifications and export licensing
requirements; (iii) escalating potential screening hits, license determinations, and red-flag
transactions to the Legal Department, the Import and Export Department, and management for
escalation and further review; (iv) continuously monitoring legal and regulatory developments in
the fields of sanctions and export controls and timely implementing new rules, including
refreshed screening of high-risk counterparties; (v) conducting ongoing sanctions and export
control compliance training for management and employees (including senior management, new
hires, and sales, finance, production, and supply staff) to ensure understanding of current
requirements, company policies, and internal control processes, and to identify, assess, and
report risks; (vi) organizing regular audit inspections of relevant business departments to assess
their compliance with sanctions and export control; and (vii) engaging external legal counsel,
where necessary, to advise the Board, senior management, and relevant personnel on sanctions
and export control risks in daily operations.
View of the Internal Control Consultant
In September 2025, we engaged an internal control consultant to review our internal control
management system relating to sanctions and export controls and to provide recommendations
for enhancement. Based on the review, the consultant identified certain deficiencies and
recommended that we strengthen its internal control measures. Since adopting the measures
after the review, the internal control consultant has not identified any significant deficiencies in
the follow-up review regarding our exposure to sanctions and export control risks. According to

TARIFFS
In 2025, the U.S. implemented a series of tariff measures, including reciprocal tariffs on
numerous trading partners. Following a period of escalated tensions, including temporary
reciprocal tariff rates as high as 125% on Chinese-origin goods, the U.S. and China announced a
90-day suspension of certain tariff measures in May 2025, which was extended in August 2025.
These agreements lowered the additional U.S. tariff rates on Chinese-origin goods from
approximately 145% (125% for reciprocal tariffs and 20% for fentanyl-related tariffs) to a
combined rate of 30%. On November 4, 2025, the United States officially announced a reduction
of fentanyl-related tariffs from 20% to 10% and maintained the suspension of heightened
reciprocal tariffs on imports from China until November 10, 2026. On February 20, 2026, the U.S.
Supreme Court issued its decision, which held that IEEPA does not give the President authority
to impose tariffs. Following such decision, the reciprocal tariffs and fentanyl-related tariffs
imposed pursuant to IEEPA was terminated. Subsequently, the U.S. imposed 10% tariff under
section 122 of the TradeAct of 1974 for a period of 150 days, effective February 24, 2026. These
rapidly evolving trade policies, along with associated geopolitical uncertainties, have created a
challenging global environment that could lead to reduced international trade, market volatility,
and increased costs.
During the Track Record Period, the aggregate revenue from our exports to the United
States represents only 6.35% of our total revenue. Given the relatively low contribution ratio, the
imposition of U.S. tariffs on the products exported to the U.S. had little impact on our overall
business operations and financial performance during the Track Record Period.
Further, we did not experience any material adverse changes in sales, order volume, selling
prices, financial performance, or received customer requests for order cancellations or
renegotiation of sales terms as a result of U.S. tariffs during the Track Record Period. All
products manufactured by our production facility in Thailand and exported to the United States
are originated in Thailand and are certified by Thailand authorities. During the Track Record
Period and as of the Latest Practicable Date, U.S. Section 301 Tariffs targeted goods of Chinese
origin and did not apply to our products manufactured by our production facility in Thailand.
Therefore, our products manufactured in Thailand were exempted from U.S. Section 301 Tariffs
during the Track Record Period and as of the Latest Practicable Date. On June 2,2026, the
United States Trade Representative (USTR) issued a determination under Section 301 of the
Trade Act of 1974 proposing an additional 12.5% Section 301 Tariff on certain imports from
Thailand and 53 other economies. This proposed tariff is subject to a public comment period
ending July 6, 2026, and public hearings scheduled for July 7, 2026, with a final determination
expected thereafter. If implemented, the applicability of this additional Section 301 Tariff to our
products would depend on whether the specific product categories fall within the scope of the
proposed duties.
Also, U.S. President agreed on a 19% U.S. “reciprocal” tariff on products from Thailand
under the IEEPA, effective fromAugust 1, 2025. Following a ruling of the U.S. Supreme Court on
February 20, 2026 that the President lacked statutory authority to impose tariffs under IEEPA, the
IEEPA-based reciprocal tariff regime was invalidated. On February 21, 2026, the U.S. President
further invoked Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 to impose a 10% tariff globally, which
applies to Thailand exports as of the Latest Practicable Date. This Section 122 tariff is statutorily
limited to 150 days and is scheduled to expire around July 2026 unless extended by the U.S.
Congress or replaced by other tariff measures. Meanwhile, as of the Latest Practicable Date, the

Our products are usually stored in our own warehouses located in our production bases

the third-party logistics service providers periodically on their performance and compliance with

agreements with our logistics service providers on an annual basis. Our logistics service
providers bear the risks associated with the transportation of our products.

experienced any significant delay or inappropriate handling of goods that materially and
adversely affected our business operations.

We have engaged an independent transfer pricing advisor, Ernst & Young (China) Advisory
Limited Beijing Branch Office (the “Transfer PricingAdvisor”) to review and assess whether our
Group’s intra-group cross-border transfer pricing arrangements meet the arm’s length principle
based on Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development Transfer Pricing Guidelines
for Multinational Enterprises and Tax Administrations, 20 January, 2022 (“OECD Transfer
Pricing Guidelines”). The Transfer Pricing Advisor reviewed the Intra-Group Transactions,
conducted functional & risk analysis, business analysis, and comparability analysis, and
evaluated whether the price or profit level of the Intra-Group Transactions met the price or profit
level required by the arm’s length principle under appropriate transfer pricing methods.
– 181 –

=== PAGE 191 ===
BUSINESS
Our Transfer Pricing Advisor selected the Transactional Net Margin Method (“TNMM”) and
the Comparable Uncontrolled Price Method (“CUP”) as the appropriate transfer pricing methods
to assess whether the transfer pricing arrangements related to the Intra-GroupTransactions were
consistent with the arm’s length principle.
In accordance with the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines, when selecting a transfer pricing
method, enterprises should choose the approach that best accurately reflects the arm’s length
principle, based on the nature of the transaction, functional risk analysis, and the reliability of
available data. The Transfer Pricing Advisor determined the selection of different transfer pricing
methods by applying these principles to the specific characteristics, functional risk profiles, and
availability of reliable comparable data for each related-party transaction, thereby verifying the
reasonableness of the transfer pricing arrangements across various types of Intra-Group
Transactions. The CUP method evaluates the price charged in a controlled transaction with
reference to the price charged in comparable uncontrolled transactions. According to the OECD
Guidelines, where it is possible to locate comparable uncontrolled transactions, the CUP method
is preferable over the other methods. The TNMM tests the arm’s-length character of transfer
prices in a controlled transaction by comparing the operating profits earned by one of the parties
engaged in controlled transactions to the operating profits earned by uncontrolled parties
engaged in similar business activities. The TNMM may be used for all types of related party
transactions. This differentiated transfer pricing methodology ensures that each type of
Intra-Group Transaction is evaluated using the appropriate transfer pricing methods to assess
whether the transfer pricing arrangements related to the Intra-Group Transactions were
consistent with the arm’s length principle.
When applying TNMM, a range of reasonable profit levels was determined by reference to
the profit levels of comparable companies. The Transfer Pricing Advisor has selected operating
margin (“OM”), mark-up on total cost (“MTC”), or berry ratio as the profit level indicator to test on
segmental or overall business profit level of Chaozhou Three-Circle, Nanchong Three-Circle,
Deyang Three-Circle, Hong Kong Three-Circle, Glory Winner during the Track Record Period.
When applying CUP, the prices charged by the related parties in the sale of goods will be
compared with the prices charged by unrelated parties in the sale of identical or similar goods,
taking into account key functional, asset, and risk profiles, as well as the terms and conditions of
the transactions. Our Transfer Pricing Advisor selected the CUP method to assess the arm’s
length nature of Vermes Germany’s pricing in transactions with its subgroup entities.
Based on the above analysis, the Transfer Pricing Advisor is of the view that our pricing
arrangements in relation to major intra-group cross border transactions have been carried out in
line with the arm’s length principle under the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines, and there is no
material transfer pricing risk identified in relation to Intra-Group Transactions of our Group during
the Track Record Period.
Although we believe our transfer pricing arrangements for Intra-Group Transactions have
reasonable technical basis and have been carried out in accordance with the arm’s length
principle, the tax treatment of these transactions may still be subject to interpretation by the
respective tax authorities in Mainland China and overseas. There is no assurance that the tax
authorities will not subsequently challenge our transfer pricing position or that the relevant
regulations or standards governing such arrangements will not be subject to future changes. If
any competent tax authority in the Mainland China or overseas later determines that our transfer
pricing arrangements do not comply with the relevant transfer pricing laws and regulations, we
may face adverse tax consequences, including additional taxes, interests or penalties, which
may result in a higher overall tax liability for us and may adversely affect our business, financial
condition and performance.

DATAPRIVACYAND CYBERSECURITY
We generally do not collect or process individual customers’ personal information since our
customers are brand companies rather than individuals. We also do not have any cross-border
data transaction. During the Track Record Period, we had complied with applicable laws and
regulations related to cybersecurity and data protection in all material aspects.
We have complied with the applicable data security and personal information protection
laws and regulations in all material aspects during the Track Record Period. We did not
experience any material security breach or data loss during theTrack Record Period. Particularly,
as further advised by local counsels, our directors are of the view that we have complied with the
applicable data security and personal information protection laws and regulations inThailand and
Germany in all material aspects during the Track Record Period.
We have established a comprehensive data compliance system that consists of
organizational structure and internal policies. Our information technology department, together
with our legal and compliance functions, is responsible for developing and implementing our
policies and procedures relating to cybersecurity and data security, with designated data owners
for critical systems who approve access rights and conduct regular permission reviews. Our
procedures ensure that we have a comprehensive set of protocols covering the prevention of
data breaches, immediate action and response in case of data incidents and post-incident
assessment and analysis, and we maintain layered technical and administrative controls,
including network segmentation, role-based access control, multi-factor authentication for
privileged accounts, encryption of data at rest and in transit where applicable, system and
database logging with periodic review, and regular vulnerability scanning and patch management
on key servers and applications. In addition, we conduct annual trial runs of data breach
incidents to test our data protection mechanism and provide various data security trainings to our
employees to ensure that our employees are well aware of our data security policies and their
responsibilities in terms of data protection. With respect to data storage, our core business
systems are hosted in secured on-premises servers located in the PRC, supported by
documented data backup and disaster recovery procedures that include scheduled encrypted
backups, off-site storage within the PRC and recovery time objectives for key systems that are
reviewed and tested periodically.
Our PRC legal advisor is of the view that, during the Track Record Period, we complied with
applicable PRC laws and regulations with respect to cybersecurity, personal data protection and
data security in all material respects.
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
We have utilized various information technology systems covering all material aspects of
our operations, including sales, supply chain management, inventory management, production
and quality control. Our IT department is responsible for developing and maintaining these
systems to support our business growth and tailor them to our specific needs. Our main
information technology systems include the following:
ERP system. Our enterprise resource planning (“ERP”) helps us integrate the core
business processes of various departments, including financial management, supply chain,
production and inventory. It can provide real-time data analysis, reduce costs, enhance
operational efficiency and support our decision-making process, thereby increasing our flexibility
and competitiveness.
– 183 –

=== PAGE 193 ===
BUSINESS
MES. Our manufacturing execution system (“MES”) serves as a crucial bridge between the
ERP and our production department. Its core functions include production scheduling, resource
management, quality control, data collection and real-time monitoring of plant personnel,
equipment and materials. It assists us in conducting timely checks, enhancing production
efficiency, and minimizing downtime and production errors, thereby optimizing our production
processes and improving our resource utilization.
WMS. Our WMS optimizes inbound and outbound logistics and inventory management. By
reducing storage costs, improving task processing speed and enhancing warehouse space
utilization, it improves warehouse efficiency, reduces errors and ensures our inventory data
accuracy.
OA system. Our office automation (“OA”) system is primarily utilized for daily office
management. It streamlines routine administrative tasks, enhances communication and improves
overall organizational efficiency by providing a centralized platform for document management,
scheduling and internal collaboration.
CRM system. Our customer relationship management (“CRM”) system manages and
analyzes customer interactions and data throughout the customer lifecycle. Its main functions
include contact management, sales automation and customer service. It organizes customer
information, automating marketing tasks, tracking customer interactions, and providing insights
into customer behavior and preferences.
SRM system. Our supplier relationship management (“SRM”) system enhances
procurement efficiency and strengthens supply chain stability through functionalities such as
supplier information management, supplier sourcing and onboarding, procurement and contract
management, and supplier performance management.

Social Insurance and Housing Provident Funds
Companies with operations in Chinese Mainland are required to contribute to a number of
social insurance funds, including funds for pension insurance, unemployment insurance, basic
medical insurance, work-related injury insurance, maternity insurance, and housing provident
fund on behalf of employees in Chinese Mainland. During the Track Record Period, we and our
PRC subsidiaries fail to make adequate contribution to social insurance and housing provident
fund for our employees. Our contribution shortfall amounted to RMB3.0 million, RMB2.2 million
and RMB2.6 million, accounting for 0.05%, 0.03% and 0.03% of our revenue in 2023, 2024 and
2025, respectively. We are of the view that such contribution shortfall will not have any material
adverse impact on our business and operations. As a result, no provisions have been made in
relation to the inadequate contributions. We were not subject to fines and other regulatory
actions due to such inadequacy contribution during the Track Record Period. As advised by our
PRC LegalAdviser, the applicable penalties are imposed on an entity-by-entity basis and vary by
type of non-compliance and its duration: according to the PRC Social Insurance Law, (a) for
social insurance fund contributions that we did not promptly pay in full, the relevant PRC
authorities may demand that we pay the outstanding social insurance contributions within a
stipulated deadline and we may be liable for a late payment fee equal to 0.05% of the outstanding
contribution amount for each day of delay; and (b) if we fail to make such payments within the
stipulated deadline, we may be liable to a fine of one to three times the outstanding contribution
amount. Therefore, the potential maximum penalty to which we may be subject, being three times
the outstanding contribution amount, would amount to RMB8.1 million, RMB6.1 million and
RMB7.3 million, accounting for 0.14%, 0.08%, and 0.08% of our revenue in 2023, 2024, and
2025, respectively, excluding any late payment fees.
If the relevant authorities order us to pay the shortfall of social insurance and/or housing
provident funds or take rectification measures in accordance with applicable laws and
regulations, we will make such payments or take such rectification measures promptly within the
specified period to avoid such penalties for overdue payment.
According to the Social Insurance Law of the PRC and the Regulations on the
Administration of Housing Provident Fund, human resources and social security bureaus and
housing provident fund management centers are the competent authorities for employee social
insurance and housing provident fund matters. According to the interviews conducted by our
PRC Legal Adviser and the Sole Sponsor’s PRC Legal Adviser in December 2025 with the
competent officials of the competent social insurance bureaus and housing provident fund
management centers of the relevant PRC subsidiaries, in the absence of employee complaints or
reports, such authorities generally do not initiate procedures for retrospective payments,
payments within a prescribed time limit, or penalties against us or our relevant PRC subsidiaries.
If any contribution shortfall are fully settled within the prescribed time limit, no further penalties
will be imposed. According to the compliance certificates confirming the absence of records of
– 186 –

=== PAGE 196 ===
BUSINESS
non-compliance issued by the competent social insurance and housing provident fund
authorities, during the Track Record Period, such authorities did not initiate any investigations,
recovery actions, warnings, circulars, or administrative penalties against us or our relevant PRC

orderly migration of equipment and personnel) to ensure business continuity without any material
impact on our operations or financial results.
We intend to comply with the lease registration requirement for all agreements to which we
are a party by 2027. However, since the filing process requires coordination between the parties,
there is a risk that the counterparty may fail to cooperate or complete the registration in a timely
manner. To address this, we will take steps to facilitate timely completion of lease registrations
and factor the counterparty’s cooperation with the registration process into our criteria for
selecting leased properties in the future.

management structure. Our Board, as the highest governance body for our ESG management, is
responsible for formulating, overseeing and reviewing our ESG strategy, including strategic
direction, target setting and key policies, as well as identifying and evaluating ESG-related risks
and opportunities to ensure that the impact of these factors on our long-term development is
adequately considered.
We have established an ESG working group and engaged external consultant to identify
and monitor ESG-related risks and opportunities and applicable regulatory and supervisory
requirements. We adopt stakeholder engagement as our core principle, conduct dual materiality

matrix of material issues to proactively address current and anticipated challenges and
implement the ESG policies and strategies designated by the Board.
Moreover, with the implementation of comprehensive risk identification and mitigation plans,
we have established scientific indicators and objectives to ensure the efficient implementation of
our green and smart strategies. We are now focusing on production safety, resource efficiency
improvement and labor rights management, among others, and have established a clear
management framework and milestones to drive continuous improvement in key ESG domains.
Up to the Latest Practicable Date, we have strictly complied with applicable ESG-related

upgrades to pollutant treatment facilities, conducting emergency drills for production safety and
implementing energy-saving retrofits for equipment. During theTrack Record Period, our ordinary

Risk Management and Measures
We proactively review our operations and industry characteristics and referencing domestic
and global ESG standards, policies, industry trends and key focus areas of global ESG ratings.
Simultaneously, we assess and rank risks across dimensions such as probability and impact
through communication with external consultants and internal discussions, and the results of
such analyses are reviewed and approved by our Strategy Committee. Accordingly, we identify
the ESG matters that have a material impact on our business and set targeted goals and
measures.
We have gathered relevant industry standards, government policies, laws, and regulations

Metrics and Targets
We employ a set of metrics, targets and measures to assess and manage the environmental
risks impacting our business. These efforts are aimed at reducing the consumption of electricity,
water, and natural gas, thereby mitigating the environmental footprint of our operations.
Greenhouse gas emissions. We aim to take 2024 as the base year and reduce the Scope
1 and Scope 2 GHG emission intensity per million RMB revenue by 8% by 2027. The key
measures to achieve this goal include investing in more energy-efficient production equipment
and waste heat recovery systems. We will also promote the low-carbon substitution of boiler fuels
and the electrification of on-site transport vehicles. Meanwhile, we plan to develop distributed
power generation projects within the factories, launch a supplier engagement programme to
encourage key suppliers to set their own emissions reduction targets and integrate their ESG
performance into the procurement assessment system. We will give preference to suppliers with
lower carbon emissions, optimize logistics and distribution routes to reduce value chain
emissions, adopt lightweight, low-carbon raw materials and recycled packaging, and establish a
carbon management mechanism to reduce GHG emissions. In addition, we will organize
carbon-reduction training for employees to embed green production principles into the
operational practices of every role.

Electricity Consumption. We aim to reduce electricity consumption per million RMB of
revenue by 10% compared to 2024 levels by December 31, 2027. To achieve this target, we have
initiated several energy-saving projects, including energy-efficient retrofits and waste heat
recovery for compressor stations, and intelligent energy-saving controls for refrigeration stations.
Additionally, we utilize ERP, CRM systems and MES for intelligent online material management to
enhance warehouse operations, thereby reducing operational time and increasing efficiency.
Operational procedures are optimized to lower energy consumption, and measures such as
maintaining optimal air conditioning temperatures, rational use of lifts, and promoting the use of
energy-efficient appliances are enforced. Meanwhile, we plan to enter into long-term power
purchase agreements in the future to achieve energy structure optimization.
Water Consumption. We aim to reduce water consumption per million RMB of revenue by
12% compared to 2024 levels by December 31, 2027. Measures to achieve this target include
implementing water-saving projects and recycling and reusing water. We have established a
dedicated wastewater recovery system to treat wastewater generated during production and then
reuse it in facilities such as cooling towers and brazing furnaces. Additionally, water valves in
less frequented public areas are turned off, and water-saving signs are posted to encourage
reduced water usage.
Social Responsibility
Employment
Human resources are particularly important to achieve the long-term sustainable
development of the Company. We are committed to creating a diverse, equal,
personality-respecting, positive and self-transcending work environment and development
platform for our employees. Our employment management measures include but are not limited
to: (i) ensuring no discrimination in employment, compensation, training, and promotion
opportunities based on race, religion, gender, nationality, age, marital status, or disability; (ii)
strictly prohibiting the employment of child labor and any form of forced labor; (iii) safeguarding
employee rights concerning compensation, working hours, rest and leave, occupational safety,
health, and training; (iv) promoting work-life balance by offering meal subsidies, housing
allowances, holiday benefits, and organizing activities such as expert medical consultations and
childcare services; and (v) lowering employee turnover through regular monitoring of turnover
rates, analysis of reasons for employee departures and timely adjustment to remuneration,
benefits and management policies.
Health and Safety
We adhere to the safety management policy of “safety first, prevention-oriented,
comprehensive management and continuous improvement” and comply with the relevant national
guidelines, policies, laws and regulations on work safety. Our health and safety goal is to achieve
zero recognized occupational diseases and prevent any serious or higher-level workplace safety
incidents each year. We have established a Work Safety Committee, set up a safety
management organization and implemented a company-wide work safety accountability system.
We have obtained certification under the ISO 45001 occupational health and safety management
system and we actively formulate work safety and occupational health policies and procedures,
including the Safety Management Provisions, the Safety Monitoring and Measurement Control
Procedure, the Control Procedure for Safety Objectives, Indicators and Management Programs,
and the Occupational Health and Safety Management Manual. During the Track Record Period,
we did not experience any major violations of occupational health and safety regulations.

OVERVIEW
Rooted in our “materials” capabilities, we focus on electronic ceramic materials and
components, with over fifty-five years of operating history. We have concentrated on electronic
ceramic materials and components throughout our history. We have built a product portfolio
across four categories — electronic and ceramic materials, electronic components,
telecommunication (“telecom”) components and equipment components — forming a business
framework that spans foundational materials, critical components and high-end devices and
assemblies across key application areas including telecom, AI and data centers, consumer
electronics, automotive electronics, semiconductor manufacturing and packaging, new energy
and intelligent industrial control.
Since the listing of our A Shares on the ChiNext of the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2014,
we have recorded steady revenue growth and maintained solid profitability. Our revenue was
RMB5,681.5 million, RMB7,266.1 million and RMB8,868.5 million in 2023, 2024 and 2025,
respectively. Our gross profit was RMB2,154.1 million, RMB2,975.3 million and RMB3,542.8
million for the same years. Our net profit was RMB1,583.2 million, RMB2,190.2 million and
RMB2,617.0 million, and our net cash generated from operating activities was RMB1,719.0
million, RMB2,403.1 million and RMB2,877.6 million for the same years, respectively. We believe
these results reflect our capability in sustainable value creation over the long term.
SIGNIFICANT FACTORSAFFECTING OUR RESULTS OF OPERATIONS
We believe there are several important factors that have affected and that we expect to
continue to affect our results of operations:
End market demand
The demand for our products, which are primarily components and materials, is largely
driven by demand for the end-products. We have a broad product portfolio strategically targeted
at various key end markets, including applications for telecom, AI and data centers, consumer
electronics, automotive electronics, semiconductor manufacturing and packaging, new energy
and intelligent industrial control.

Driven by growth of these end markets, the size of the electronic ceramic material and
component markets we operate in are expected to grow continuously, according to Frost &
Sullivan:
• the global core electronic ceramic material market is expected to increase from
RMB27.8 billion in 2026 to RMB43.1 billion in 2030 at a CAGR of 11.6%.
• the global core ceramic electronic component market is expected to increase from
RMB194.6 billion in 2026 to RMB256.8 billion in 2030 at a CAGR of 7.2%.
• the global core ceramic telecom component market is expected to increase from
RMB53.4 billion in 2026 to RMB75.9 billion in 2030 at a CAGR of 9.2%.
• the global core ceramic equipment component market is expected to increase from
RMB62.9 billion in 2026 to RMB98.6 billion in 2030 at a CAGR of 11.9%.
The continued growth of our business will depend on our ability to further penetrate existing
end markets and expand into new end markets to capture these growing market opportunities.
For example, we are expanding our market shares in the high-end MLCC in automotive, AI data
center and industrial control sectors. The progress and success of such expansion and growth
will affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Maintaining and growing relationship with our customers
Our results of operations have been and are expected to be affected by our ability to
maintain and grow our relationship with end market customers. Demand for our products from
end market customers is impacted by a number of factors, including overall macro-economic
conditions and the quality of our products. For example, unfavorable changes in global economic
conditions and consumer spending could negatively affect demand for consumer electronics and
automotives, which in turn will negatively affect our customers’ demand for our products and
therefore our results of operations.
Additionally, to stay ahead of competition in end markets, our customers may require us to
(i) advance our technologies and production techniques to develop products that meet our
customers’evolving requirements and (ii) lower our product prices, which we will need to mitigate
through cost reduction measures such as improving production efficiency. Our ability to achieve
technological innovation and to enhance our production efficiency will affect our customers’
demand for our products as well as our profit margins.
Product mix and pricing
We generate revenue from electronic and ceramic materials, electronic components,
telecom components, equipment components and other products. These categories and the
products within them have different pricing and margin characteristics. Our profitability is affected
by our ability to price our products to achieve our intended profit margins, and our results of
operation for a given period will be affected by the mix of our products.
• Electronic and ceramic materials include multiple product families, materials systems,
and technical specifications. Their prices and gross margin profiles vary by formulation
complexity, performance grade, and application requirements, as well as by changes in
supply–demand conditions and raw material costs.

FINANCIAL INFORMATION
• Electronic components’ gross profit maintained a growth momentum during the Track
Record Period, supported by favorable supply–demand dynamics in selected product
lines and our emphasis on product quality and reliability. However, margins for
products within this sector can fluctuate, driven by differences in product mix and
specifications.
• Telecom components margins vary with the mix between products used in different end
applications and carried different specifications, and with shifts in demand from
communications and data center applications.
• Equipment components margins vary with the mix between standard products and
high-spec components, and with shifts in demand across end-markets and lifecycle
phases.
During the Track Record Period, the gross margin for electronic and ceramic materials
continued to decrease while its average selling price continued to increase, due to a shift in
product mix toward higher-priced but also higher-cost items and the timing of cost pass-throughs.
Specifically, we sold a greater proportion of advanced materials, including substrates and pastes
that command higher selling prices. In addition, increases in key raw material costs and
consumables were not fully reflected in customer pricing within the same period due to
qualification and contract cycles, resulting in temporary pressure on gross margin.
Average selling price and gross margin for electronic components was relatively low in 2023
as a result of product mix changes and weak industry demand during the year. Within electronic
components, MLCC served as a key driver of revenue and profitability growth since 2023.
Higher-specification MLCCs for automotive, industrial control, AI and data center applications
generally exhibit stronger profitability compared with general-purpose MLCCs, subject to
utilization, yield, and program pricing dynamics.
Equipment components generally carried higher gross margins during the Track Record
Period primarily because these products have high technical barriers and longer qualification
cycles, leading to consistent pricing and reduced exposure to short-term commodity cost swings.
Recurring demand for spares and services associated with equipment components also
supported our gross margin in this sector.
Ability to control cost of sales
Our cost of sales mainly includes costs of raw materials used in the production of our
products, as well as associated labor and manufacturing costs. Our ability to control our cost of
sales is crucial in maintaining our desired profitability.
We have adopted an integrated production model, from ceramic base material production,
the development and assembly of manufacturing equipment for our products, to the production of
our final products. This model lowers our cost of sales. Our ability to continue to optimize
efficiency across these production areas will affect our cost of sales.
On the other hand, higher raw material or labor costs due to shortage or other market
dynamics may reduce our gross margins if we are unable to mitigate these additional costs
through higher selling prices or increased production efficiency.
Changes in technologies
Our products are applied in a wide range of electronic, optical and other devices, which are
characterized by rapidly changing technologies aimed at enhancing functionality and
performance, as well as meeting evolving industry standards.

MATERIALACCOUNTING POLICIESAND ESTIMATES
Note 4 to “Appendix I — Accountants’ Report” to this prospectus sets forth certain material
accounting policy information, which are important for understanding our financial conditions and
results of operations.
Revenue from contracts with customers
Revenue is recognised to depict the transfer of promised goods or services to customers in
an amount that reflects the consideration to which the entity expects to be entitled in exchange
for those goods or services. Specifically, the Group uses a 5-step approach to revenue
recognition:
• Step 1: Identify the contract(s) with a customer
• Step 2: Identify the performance obligations in the contract
• Step 3: Determine the transaction price
• Step 4:Allocate the transaction price to the performance obligations in the contract
• Step 5: Recogniserevenuewhen(oras)theentitysatisfiesaperformanceobligation.
The Group recognised revenue when (or as) a performance obligation is satisfied, i.e. when
“control” of the goods or services underlying the particular performance obligation is transferred
to customers.
A performance obligation represents a good or service (or a bundle of goods or services)
that is distinct or a series of distinct goods or services that are substantially the same.
Control is transferred over time and revenue is recognised over time by reference to the
progress towards complete satisfaction of the relevant performance obligation if one of the
following criteria is met:
• The customer simultaneously receives and consumes the benefits provided by the
Group’s performance as the Group performs;
• The Group’s performance creates or enhances an asset that the customer controls as
the asset is created or enhanced; or
– 199 –

=== PAGE 209 ===
FINANCIAL INFORMATION
• The Group’s performance does not create an asset with an alternative use to the
Group and the Group has an enforceable right to payment for performance completed
to date.
Otherwise, revenue is recognised at a point in time when the customer obtains control of the
distinct goods or service.
Revenue is measured based on the consideration to which the Group expects to be entitled
in a contract with a customer, excludes amounts collected on behalf of third parties, discounts
and sales related taxes.
The Group recognised revenue from sales of electronic and ceramic materials, electronic
components, telecom components and equipment components and other products.
Sales of electronic and ceramic materials, electronic components, telecom components
and equipment components and other products
Revenue from sales of electronic and ceramic materials, electronic components, telecom
components and equipment components and other products between the Group and its
customers generally only includes a performance obligation for the transfer of goods, which is
recognised when the performance obligation has been satisfied at a point in time.
Revenue from local sale of goods is recognised at a point in time when the Group has
delivered the products to the customers in accordance with the contract terms, and has been
received and accepted by the customers.
Revenue from export sale of goods is recognised at a point in time upon completion of
export declaration, when control of the goods is transferred.
Some of our accounting policies require us to apply estimates and assumptions as well as
complex judgments relating to accounting items. The estimates and assumptions we use and the
judgments we make in applying our accounting policies have a significant impact on our financial
position and results of operations. Our management continually evaluates such estimates,
assumptions and judgments based on past experiences and other factors, including industry
practices and expectations of future events that are believed to be reasonable under the
circumstances. There has not been any material deviation between our management’s estimates
or assumptions and actual results, and we have not made any material changes to these
estimates or assumptions during the Track Record Period. We do not expect any material
changes in these estimates and assumptions in the foreseeable future. See Note 5 to “Appendix I
—Accountants’Report.”

During the Track Record Period, the gross margin for electronic and ceramic materials
continued to decrease while its average selling price continued to increase, due to a shift in
product mix toward higher-priced but also higher-cost items and the timing of cost pass-throughs.
Specifically, we sold a greater proportion of advanced materials, including substrates and pastes
that command higher selling prices. In addition, increases in key raw material costs and
consumables were not fully reflected in customer pricing within the same period due to
qualification and contract cycles, resulting in temporary pressure on gross margin.
The gross margin for electronic components increased from 2023 to 2024 due to increase in
average selling price and shipment volume which diluted fixed manufacturing overheads. The
gross margin for electronic components slightly decreased from 2024 to 2025 due to change of
specifications in 2025.
During the Track Record Period, the gross margin for telecom components continued to
increase primarily due to increase in average selling price and sales volume, reflecting improved
economies of scale and strong market demand.
Equipment components carried higher gross margins during the Track Record Period
primarily because these products have high technical barriers and longer qualification cycles,
leading to consistent pricing and reduced exposure to short-term commodity cost swings.
Recurring demand for spares and services associated with equipment components also
supported our gross margin in this sector.

Our revenue increased by 22.1% from RMB7,266.1 million in 2024 to RMB8,868.5 million in
2025, primarily due to increases in revenue from the sales of electronic and ceramic materials,
electronic components and telecom components.
Electronic and Ceramic Materials
Our revenue from sales of electronic and ceramic materials increased by 16.8% from
RMB1,677.2 million in 2024 to RMB1,959.4 million in 2025, primarily due to the increase in
average selling price from RMB686.4 per unit to RMB854.4 per unit, which in turn reflects an
increase in price of raw materials and a change in our product mix whereby resulted in revenue
contribution from certain higher-value materials increased due to strong demand. Raw material
prices increased mainly in high-purity ceramic and metal powders and specialty additives used in
higher-spec formulations, and we adjusted pricing to reflect these input changes. The mix
upgrade was driven by customer programs that required tighter tolerances and enhanced
reliability specifications for materials used in advanced packaging and power electronics, which
carry higher value but are manufactured in smaller batches with stricter process controls. The
increase in our average selling price offset a slight decrease in our sales volume from 2.4 million
units to 2.3 million units, which was due to overall weaker downstream demand.
Electronic Components
Our revenue from sales of electronic components increased by 43.9% from RMB2,298.2
million in 2024 to RMB3,308.1 million in 2025, primarily due to the increase in sales volume from
33.7 million units to 48.8 million units, reflecting stronger downstream demand for MLCCs in
consumer electronics, home appliances,AI and data centers, and automotive electronics, as well
– 207 –

=== PAGE 217 ===
FINANCIAL INFORMATION
as customers’ increased preference for localized products amid geopolitical and policy factors.
The volume increase reflected multi-end-market momentum: in consumer electronics and home
appliances, customers resumed replenishment after prior destocking; in AI and data centers, we
benefited from higher content per server driven by power management and decoupling needs;
and in automotive electronics, platform upgrades and penetration of electrified and intelligent
features increased the number of MLCCs per vehicle. We also broadened our offering in certain
case sizes and reliability grades, which expanded accessible demand and supported the higher
shipment run-rate.
Telecom Components
Our revenue from sales of telecom components increased by 12.5% from RMB2,306.0
million in 2024 to RMB2,594.3 million in 2025, primarily due to the increase in sales volume from
2.0 million units to 2.2 million units. Growth was supported by continued build-out of high-speed
optical links for data centers and backbone networks, where demand for ceramic ferrules and
PKG products with low insertion loss and high concentricity tolerance remained firm.
Equipment Components
Our revenue from sales of equipment components increased by 12.1% from RMB536.8
million in 2024 to RMB601.8 million in 2025, primarily due to the increase in average selling price
from RMB62,249.1 per unit to RMB76,336.5 per unit, while sales volume remained stable.
Other Products
Our revenue from sales of other products decreased by 9.6% from RMB447.9 million in
2024 to RMB405.0 million in 2025, primarily due to decrease in sales volume of our ceramic
appearance parts attributable to completion of a customized product project in 2024.

Our gross profit increased by 19.1% from RMB2,975.3 million in 2024 to RMB3,542.8 million
in 2025, primarily due to increases in gross profit from sales of electronic components and
telecom components. Our gross margin remained stable at 40.9% and 39.9%, respectively,
reflecting the combined effects of scale benefits in components and a modest margin contraction
in electronic and ceramic materials.
Electronic and Ceramic Materials
Our gross profit from sales of electronic and ceramic materials increased by 8.4% from
RMB661.6 million in 2024 to RMB717.5 million in 2025, primarily due to an increase in revenue.
Gross margin from sales of electronic and ceramic materials decreased slightly from 39.4%
in 2024 to 36.6% in 2025 primarily as a result of higher raw materials price and an increase in
revenue contribution from lower value materials. The margin movement mainly reflected higher
input costs for key raw materials, including metal powders, which rose during the period and
were only partially offset by pricing adjustments. In addition, a change in product mix also
contributed to the change in gross margin. For details of the margin profile of our electronic and
ceramic materials, see “— Significant FactorsAffecting Our Results of Operations — Product Mix
and Pricing.”
Electronic Components
Our gross profit from sales of electronic components increased by 36.6% from RMB1,000.3
million in 2024 to RMB1,366.4 million in 2025, primarily due to an increase in revenue, partially
offset by a decrease in gross margin from 43.5% in 2024 to 41.3% in 2025, which was due to a
decrease in average selling price driven by change of specifications with an increased
contribution from smaller-sized products that are priced at relatively lower levels.
During the period, shipments to consumer electronics and home appliances recovered
alongside strong growth inAI and data center and automotive applications. Higher sales volumes
reduced the per-unit allocation of fixed costs, supporting gross profit growth. This was offset by
the change product specification mix, with an increased proportion of smaller-sized products
priced at a relatively lower levels, resulting in a decrease in the gross margin.
Telecom Components
Our gross profit from sales of telecom components increased by 13.2% from RMB977.4
million in 2024 to RMB1,106.1 million in 2025, primarily due to increases in revenue and gross
margin from 42.4% to 42.6%. The increase in gross margin was due to the increased sales
volume which improved our economies of scale.
– 209 –

=== PAGE 219 ===
FINANCIAL INFORMATION
The margin improvement was driven by increased sales volume that enhanced economies
of scale in core processes such as precision molding, grinding and inspection, which reduced
average manufacturing overhead per unit. We also recorded a greater contribution from ceramic
ferrules and PKG products used in data centers and 5G equipment with tighter tolerance
requirements, which supported process yields after prior qualifications and translated into
improved cost efficiency at higher run-rates. Procurement and planning efficiencies associated
with higher throughput further contributed to the margin expansion.
Equipment Components
Our gross profit from sales of equipment components increased by 8.8% from RMB319.3
million in 2024 to RMB347.5 million in 2025, primarily due to an increase in revenue. Gross
margin from sales of equipment components decreased slightly from 59.5% in 2024 to 57.7% in
2025 primarily as a result of increased per unit costs attributable to the change of specifications
in 2025.
Other Products
Our gross profit from the sales of other products decreased by 67.9% from RMB16.6 million
in 2024 to RMB5.3 million in 2025, primarily due to a decrease in revenue and gross margin from
3.7% in 2024 to 1.3% in 2025. This was primarily the result of loss of economies of scale as lower
sales and fixed manufacturing costs led to increase in per-unit costs.
Other Income, Gains and Losses, Net
Our net other income, gains and losses increased by 12.4% from RMB673.8 million in 2024
to RMB757.1 million in 2025, primarily due to (i) an increase in government grants from
RMB240.6 million in 2024 to RMB359.9 million in 2025 due to new government grants received in
2025, (ii) an increase in rental income from RMB23.8 million to RMB37.7 million and (iii) an
increase in sales of basic and wasted material, net from RMB81.3 million in 2024 to RMB98.8
million in 2025, which was partially offset by a decrease in others of RMB49.4 million, attributable
to increased exchange losses on US dollar and decrease in value-added tax additional
deduction.

Our revenue increased by 27.9% from RMB5,681.5 million in 2023 to RMB7,266.1 million in
2024, primarily due to the increase in revenue from electronic components and telecom
components. The growth reflected both higher shipment volumes into recovering end markets
and a favorable shift in product mix toward higher-specification products in key programs.
Electronic and Ceramic Materials
Our revenue from sales of electronic and ceramic materials increased by 8.3% from
RMB1,548.7 million in 2023 to RMB1,677.2 million in 2024, primarily due to an increase in
average selling price from RMB588.7 per unit to RMB686.4 per unit, as we increased our selling
price in response to a change in product mix and to a lesser extent, an increase in price of raw
materials. Sales volume remained stable at 2.6 million units and 2.4 million units, respectively.
The mix shift was driven by customer programs in advanced packaging and power electronics
that required higher-value formulations and tighter process controls, which supported pricing,
while some general-purpose applications saw slower offtake and did not materially contribute to
volume growth.
Electronic Components
Our revenue from sales of electronic components increased by 46.2% from RMB1,572.3
million in 2023 to RMB2,298.2 million in 2024, primarily due to the increase in sales volume from
24.5 million units to 33.7 million units, which was driven by increase in our market share of
MLCCs in downstream industries, such as consumer electronics, automotive, AI data center and
industrial control. The average selling price also increased from RMB64.2 per unit to RMB68.2
per unit, due to favorable product mix change — specifically, a higher proportion of higher-priced
MLCCs in our sales. The volume growth reflected improved delivery responsiveness, while the
mix uplift was supported by higher content per device inAI and automotive applications.
Telecom Components
Our revenue from sales of telecom components increased by 30.5% from RMB1,766.8
million in 2023 to RMB2,306.0 million in 2024, primarily due to an increase in both sales volume
and average selling price, reflecting increase in market demand and favorable product mix.
Growth was supported by continued build-out of high-speed optical networks and data-center
interconnects, with a greater share of ceramic ferrules and PKG products meeting higher
tolerance specifications, which contributed to the improvement in average selling price.
Equipment Components
Our revenue from sales of equipment components increased by 12.3% from RMB478.0
million in 2023 to RMB536.8 million in 2024, primarily due to an increase in average selling price
from RMB56,711.5 per unit to RMB62,249.1 per unit, while sales volume increased from 8,000

higher proportion of advanced piezo microdispensing system and improved product mix, as well
as our efforts to develop new customers and new projects.
Other Products
Our revenue from sales of other products increased by 41.9% from RMB315.7 million in

Our gross profit increased from RMB2,154.1 million in 2023 to RMB2,975.3 million in 2024.
Our gross margin increased from 37.9% in 2023 to 40.9% in 2024.
Electronic and Ceramic Materials
Our gross profit from sales of electronic and ceramic materials was RMB662.2 million in
2023 and RMB661.6 million in 2024, while gross margin decreased from 42.8% to 39.4%. The
decrease mainly reflected higher costs of high-purity ceramic and metal powders and certain
specialty additives used in higher-spec formulations during 2024, together with a greater
proportion of materials supplied for advanced packaging and power electronics programs that
involve tighter process controls, smaller batch runs and additional reliability testing. These
factors raised per-unit processing costs and offset the benefit from higher average selling prices
– 213 –

=== PAGE 223 ===
FINANCIAL INFORMATION
associated with product mix upgrades. Pricing remained disciplined and supported by ongoing
customer qualifications, but could not fully neutralize the input cost increases and the higher
manufacturing intensity of premium materials.
Electronic Components
Our gross profit from sales of electronic components increased from RMB437.9 million in
2023 to RMB1,000.3 million in 2024, while gross margin increased from 27.8% to 43.5%. The
improvement was driven by a substantial increase in shipment volumes that elevated factory
utilization and diluted fixed manufacturing overheads, alongside a richer sales mix. Demand
strengthened in automotive,AI and data center and industrial control applications, which typically
require higher-reliability grades and larger case sizes with higher unit values. Customer
qualifications completed in late 2023 translated into sustained volume orders in 2024, and our
MLCC products with wider spectrum of capacitance and voltage specifications enabled us to
capture a greater share of orders. These factors supported average selling prices and yields at
scale, contributing to the step-up in gross margin.
Telecom Components
Our gross profit from sales of telecom components increased from RMB702.7 million in
2023 to RMB977.4 million in 2024, primarily due to the increase in revenue. Gross margin
increased from 39.8% to 42.4%. The margin improvement reflected stronger market demand for
ceramic ferrules and PKG products used in data centers and 5G deployments, which supported
higher run-rates and improved utilization across precision molding, grinding and inspection
processes. As volumes increased, we achieved better operating efficiency and more stable
yields, and a larger share of orders met higher tolerance specifications that carry stronger unit
economics, together resulting in margin expansion.
Equipment Components
Our gross profit from sales of equipment components increased from RMB285.0 million in
2023 to RMB319.3 million in 2024, primarily due to the increase in revenue. Gross margin
remained stable at 59.6% and 59.5%, respectively.
Other Products
Our gross profit from sales of other products decreased from RMB66.4 million in 2023 to
RMB16.6 million in 2024, while gross margin decreased from 21.0% to 3.7%, primarily due to
changes in product mix and supply-demand dynamic of our other products as our other products
were largely customized with relatively short product life cycles and lower input-output ratio. As
the products manufactured vary across different periods depending on project timelines, the
product produced in 2024 including ceramic appearance parts had a lower gross margin profile
than that in 2023. Specifically, each of our ceramic appearance parts for smartphones and
watches projects has distinct selling prices and cost structures. The gross margin of these
projects was lower in 2024 than in 2023, primarily because the combined effect of reduced
production yield rates and higher per-unit costs on projects executed in 2024 outpaced the
increase in selling prices. The projects we executed in 2023 were primarily for smartphone back
cover, a subcategory of ceramic appearance parts for smartphones, which had higher gross
margin as a result of our stronger bargaining power.

LIQUIDITYAND CAPITAL RESOURCES
During the Track Record Period, we financed our operations primarily through a
combination of cash generated from operating activities and bank deposits. As of December 31,
2025, we had cash and cash equivalents of RMB2,285.4 million. Going forward, we believe our
liquidity requirements will be satisfied by using funds from a combination of cash generated from
operations and net proceeds from the Global Offering.
Taking into account the net proceeds from the Global Offering and cash generated from our
operating activities available to us, our Directors believe that we have sufficient working capital to
meet our present and future cash requirements for at least the next 12 months from the date of
publication of this Prospectus.

temperature- and humidity-controlled environments. Such storage conditions do not affect
product quality, and performance testing is re-conducted prior to shipment to ensure product
quality upon delivery.
